questions.q: A new agile project manager is trying to determine how the team is performing against the schedule for a release. Which tool will provide a deeper look into the team's progress?

o.t: Release plan.
Product roadmap.
Kanban board.
Burndown chart.

questions.e: A burndown chart is a visual tool that shows the remaining work versus the time available in a release or iteration. It provides a clear picture of the team's progress and how they are performing against the schedule. By tracking the amount of work left to be done, the burndown chart helps identify whether the team is on track to meet their goals and can highlight any deviations from the planned schedule.

questions.q: A subcontracting company is presenting its feature release A key stakeholder is asking to add a new feature to the product. How should the project manager deal with the new requirement? *

o.t: Follow the change management process and work with procurement if needed.
Engage an arbitrator to resolve any conflict while handling the new requirement.
Add the change to the next sprint to meet the customer's needs.
Allocate resources to work on the new feature immediately to complete the request.

questions.e: This approach maintains project control, assesses the impact on scope, time, cost, and resources, and ensures that all stakeholders agree on the changes. Working with procurement might be necessary if the new feature involves contractual adjustments or additional resources. This methodical approach helps manage risks and ensures the project remains aligned with its objectives.

questions.q: A member of the board of directors is the sponsor of a project that is important to the organization. This stakeholder has many other priorities and is not currently engaged in the project activities. How should the stakeholder be engaged in the project? *

o.t: Keep the stakeholder informed and consult with them based on their needs.
Involve the stakeholder in governance and decision making.
Consult with the stakeholder and increase their level of interest.
The stakeholder needs to be made aware of the project progress.

questions.e: Keeping the stakeholder informed and consulting with them based on their needs is a practical approach for stakeholders with many other priorities. This ensures they stay updated and involved without overburdening them, thus maintaining their engagement at a manageable level.

questions.q: A project manager is working on the budget for a long-term project. The project manager creates a work breakdown structure (WBS) and estimates the cost for each work package based on past projects. What else does the project manager need to do before determining the budget baseline? *

o.t: Look at a previous project to ensure the budget totals match.
Require all stakeholders to review and approve the estimates.
Revise the project timeline and scope based on the WBS.
Add contingency into the budget for inflation and other changes.

questions.e: Adding contingency into the budget is an essential step to account for uncertainties, inflation, and other potential changes that could affect project costs. This ensures that the budget is realistic and can accommodate unforeseen expenses, helping to create a more accurate and reliable budget baseline.

questions.q: A newly hired team member just joined the project team and reports directly to the project manager. In the first week, this new member tells the project manager that there is a task priority conflict with hard, dependent tasks on the critical path. What should the project manager do to handle the conflict? *

o.t: Guide the team member on how to resolve the conflict.
Analyze the project schedule and look for alternatives.
Perform crashing and/or fast tracking of the schedule.
Meet the team member and try to plan a course of action together.

questions.e: Analyzing the project schedule allows the project manager to understand the impact of the task priority conflict on the critical path and to identify possible alternatives to resolve the conflict without compromising the project timeline. This approach ensures a thorough assessment of the situation before taking any further action.

questions.q: An organization in a regulated industry has decided to switch from a predictive to an agile delivery approach. It has been decided that the ongoing projects will adopt Scrum, and the project manager is still accountable for the project outcomes. During the fourth sprint demo, the customer notices that a feature is not compliant with the regulations. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Have the team consult with the compliance officer to update the definition of done (DoD) for the user stories in the past sprint.
Have the product owner consult with the change control board (CCB) to have the necessary compliance requirements implemented.
Have the scrum master organize a weekly meeting with the compliance officer, the product owner, and the project team.
Have the product owner review the user stories in the product backlog with the compliance officer on a regular basis to identify any gaps.

questions.e: Regular review of the user stories in the product backlog with the compliance officer helps ensure that compliance requirements are identified and addressed continuously. This proactive approach minimizes the risk of non-compliance and ensures that regulatory requirements are integrated into the project from the start.

questions.q: A project team member complained to the project manager that they are not sure on the latest requirements document because it was emailed to them about one week ago. They mentioned that, in the past they worked on a document tor more than 20 hours only to find out later that another team member had already updated that same document but did not send them the latest revisions. What should the project manager do to avoid this situation in the future? *

o.t: Encourage better team communication by positioning team members closer together.
Implement a project management information system (PMIS).
Update the communications management plan to ensure correct delivery of the latest version.
Restrict team members from sending the requirements documents via email.

questions.e: Implementing a Project Management Information System (PMIS) provides a centralized platform for storing, updating, and accessing project documents. This ensures that all team members have access to the most recent versions of documents, reducing the risk of working on outdated information and enhancing overall team collaboration and efficiency.

questions.q: After completion of a project with specific users in various countries, the project manager's supervisor asks if the project users are satisfied with the way the project was run. What two actions should the project manager take? (Choose two) *

o.t: Prepare the lessons learned from the project phase.
Obtain official approval on the new process from the various countries.
Send a questionnaire to the project participants and seek their feedback.
Refer to the communications management plan.
Deliver the project materials to the users and see if they have any comments.

questions.e: A. Prepare the lessons learned from the project phase: Documenting lessons learned helps capture what went well and what didn't during the project. This information can be used to improve future projects and address any issues related to user satisfaction. C. Send a questionnaire to the project participants and seek their feedback: This action directly gathers feedback from the project users about their satisfaction and experiences with the project. It provides valuable insights into user satisfaction.

questions.q: To estimate the costs of a new project that is similar to a project that was implemented last year, the project manager meets with a group of experts from the previous project. The group uses a three-point estimating technique. The project manager submits the estimated budget to the project sponsor for approval. The project sponsor, who is new to the company, is concerned because the budget exceeded their expectations What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Review the organizational process assessment to determine if a contingency reserve was considered in the budget estimate.
Review the historical information and lessons learned from last year’s project to justify the new budget estimate.
Change the budgeting technique to a more accurate, bottom-up cost estimation.
Use soft skills to convince the project sponsor to approve the new budget estimate.

questions.e: Reviewing the historical information and lessons learned from the previous project provides a solid basis for the current budget estimate. It allows the project manager to justify the budget by showing that the estimates are based on real, documented past experiences and data, thus addressing the sponsor's concerns with evidence.

questions.q: A project manager has been asked to participate in the procurement process for a software application that allows customers to buy online e-learning courses. The project manager will take over the project once the supplier has been sourced. What should the project manager do before the project starts? *

o.t: Ensure that the requirements for the project are understood and that the objectives are verified before approval of an agreement.
Inform the project sponsor that once the agreement has been signed, there cannot be any changes to the scope of the project.
Notify the project sponsor that the project manager cannot be involved in the agreement negotiation process.
Ask the project sponsor to involve the legal department in the negotiation for the project agreement.

questions.e: Ensuring that the requirements and objectives are understood and verified before approving an agreement is crucial. This step helps in clearly defining what is expected from the project, reducing the risk of misunderstandings, and ensuring that the project starts with a well-defined scope and objectives.

questions.q: A project manager is new to hybrid project management and is worried about the project because it has a high level of requirements uncertainty. The team has experience with hybrid projects, performs daily standups, and is committed to the project. The project manager is concerned about losing control of the project and would like to have a more central role. How should the project manager address this issue? *

o.t: Modify the daily standup meetings to include project status reporting.
Escalate the issue to the change control board (CCB) and ask for advice.
Adopt the role of supporting and empowering the project team to do the work.
Change the approach for the project to a predictive approach.

questions.e: Adopting the role of supporting and empowering the project team is crucial in a hybrid project environment. It allows the project manager to facilitate and guide the team while maintaining oversight without micromanaging. This approach leverages the team's experience and commitment, ensuring that the project progresses effectively while addressing the project manager's concern about losing control.

questions.q: A technical subject matter expert (SME) identifies an occurrence that should be captured in the project's lessons learned. The SME asks the project manager to write, document and include it in the lessons learned register. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Assign the documenting task to a project team member.
Ask the SME to document and capture the occurrence.
Request the SME to wait until the project closure phase.
Take ownership of documenting this information.

questions.e: Asking the SME to document and capture the occurrence ensures that the information is recorded accurately and in detail by the person who has the most knowledge about the situation. This approach also promotes accountability and ensures that the lessons learned are comprehensive and precise.

questions.q: A project manager at a large corporation has been assigned to oversee a customer experience project. Within the project, customer satisfaction is a big issue and there are many unresolved customer queries on a daily basis. The project manager has been informed that the customer service team is overwhelmed with these unresolved queries. Which two actions should the project manager take to correct this problem? (Choose two) *

o.t: Contact the customers in batches and inform them that the issues are being worked on currently.
Confirm the issues truly exist by conducting a survey and other analyses that may detect the real issue.
Deploy solutions that will track, prioritize, and resolve queries as soon as possible.
Ask senior management to replace the customer service manager with a more qualified one.
Request that the customer service team prioritizes work on queries that are received this week.

questions.e: For a project manager overseeing a customer experience project where customer satisfaction is a significant issue, it is crucial to first confirm the existence of the issues reported by customers. Conducting a survey and other analyses helps in understanding the root cause of the customer queries and ensures that the solutions provided are targeted and effective. This approach is supported by the PMBOKGuide, which emphasizes the importance of accurate data collection and analysis for project decision-making. Once the issues are confirmed, deploying solutions that can track, prioritize, and resolve queries promptly is essential. This aligns with the principles of effective project management and business analysis, which advocate for the use of tools and techniques to manage and address stakeholder concerns efficiently. By implementing such solutions, the project manager can ensure that the customer service team is not overwhelmed and that customer satisfaction is improved.

questions.q: A marketing team is developing ideas in order to revamp an existing product. The marketing executive reaches out to the project manager to make sure that necessary measures are in place for a successful launch. On what should the project manager focus? *

o.t: Ensuring that the team is also focused on the overall change management plan.
Determining and aligning performance indicators that will help in assessing successful delivery.
Planning for regular project updates to cover the status of critical deliverables.
Ensuring that the scope management plan is in place to cover all related objectives.

questions.e: Focusing on determining and aligning performance indicators is crucial for assessing the success of the product launch. These indicators provide measurable criteria to evaluate the project's progress and outcomes, ensuring that the project delivers the desired results and meets stakeholder expectations.

questions.q: After a meeting with the customer, the project manager receives special recognition because the project is always on schedule Later that day, the project manager attends a regular project team meeting to follow up on the status of the deliverables. What should the project manager do in the project team meeting? *

o.t: Share the customer feedback with the project team.
Follow the meeting agenda and make a list of the next deliverables.
Document this feedback in the meeting minutes.
Start planning how to improve the dates of next deliverables.

questions.e: Sharing the customer feedback with the project team helps to acknowledge their hard work and dedication, boosting morale and motivation. It reinforces the positive impact of their efforts and encourages them to maintain or improve their performance.

questions.q: A retail chain is evaluating a project to replace payment systems across all its stores in multiple locations. The project does not pass the financial threshold but is also expected to increase market share, improve customer services and retain more customers. The project is planned as a phased implementation building on learning from the retrospectives during each phase. How should the business increase the value of the project? *

o.t: Quantify the expected tangible and intangible benefits in the benefits management plan for each phase.
Ask the benefits owner to reassess the identified risks that are impacting the outcomes of the financial benefits.
Consult with experts on methods to reduce costs and increase the financial value of the project.
Use a fishbone diagram to find the root cause of the lower financial benefits with the benefits owner.

questions.e: Since the project does not meet the financial threshold but is expected to deliver intangible benefits such as increasing market share, improving customer service, and retaining more customers, it is important to quantify both tangible and intangible benefits. These should be detailed in the benefits management plan for each phase, providing a clear framework to measure success and justify the project’s value over time. By breaking down the benefits into quantifiable components, the business can track progress, show incremental value, and justify the continued investment in the phased approach.

questions.q: A research and development department is planning to develop a product that will introduce a new line of business for the organization. What should the project manager do to increase the project's chances of success? *

o.t: Plan a working session focusing on the scope, vision, and mission of the initiative.
Start developing the project management plan based on a previous project template from the project management office (PMO).
Conduct benchmarking to determine the business viability of the initiative.
Conduct an impact analysis of the new initiative to determine how the project should be rolled out.

questions.e: Planning a working session that focuses on the scope, vision, and mission of the initiative ensures that all stakeholders have a clear and unified understanding of the project's goals and objectives. This alignment is crucial for guiding the project's direction and increasing its chances of success.

questions.q: A project manager led the implementation of an electronic invoicing project that has just been completed. The financial manager communicated that the team discovered three invoices with errors. Which two documents should the project manager update as soon as possible? (Choose two) *

o.t: Issue log.
Risk register.
Stakeholder register.
Change log.
Backlog register.

questions.e: A. Issue log: The issue log should be updated to document the discovered invoice errors. This log helps in tracking issues that arise during the project and ensures they are addressed and resolved. D. Change log: The change log should be updated to reflect any changes that may be required as a result of addressing the invoice errors. This ensures that all modifications to the project are documented and tracked.

questions.q: During a project status update by the project management office (PMO), the CEO is concerned that the status of all projects suddenly changed from green to red, without warning. Upper management is used to reading traditional reports related to progress and cost, and they want to continue viewing this information. How should the PMO implement a better way to report the project's health? *

o.t: Perform a root cause analysis (RCA) to find out why the status of projects is deteriorating so fast.
Explore reporting the earned value (EV) key performance indicators (KPls) using agile progress as an input.
Ask the project managers to report on their projects using a Kanban board format.
Request the program managers to be more accurate when presenting status reports.

questions.e: Reporting the earned value (EV) key performance indicators (KPIs) using agile progress as an input provides a more accurate and real-time picture of project health. This method can bridge the gap between traditional reporting and agile practices, offering upper management the detailed and insightful data they are accustomed to, while also accommodating the dynamic nature of agile projects.

questions.q: A project manager is assigned to a global project where, during the planning process, team members from different regions are not agreeing to collaborate with each other. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Review lessons learned from previous projects that used the same team.
Review the organizational culture, structure, and governance.
Coordinate a meeting to understand the situation and resolve any conflicts.
Coordinate a meeting with regional managers to ask for support.

questions.e: Coordinating a meeting to understand the situation and resolve any conflicts allows the project manager to directly address the issues causing the lack of collaboration. This approach fosters open communication, helps identify the root causes of the disagreement, and works towards finding a resolution that promotes teamwork and cooperation among the global team members.

questions.q: A project manager is tasked with managing a customer relationship management (CRM) implementation project. The project charter is approved, and the project is now in the planning phase. The project manager meets with the stakeholders several times to gather the initial requirements. However, each time they meet, the stakeholders provide additional information that is different from what they provided earlier. The stakeholders are becoming frustrated, and the sponsor is now unresponsive. What should the project manager have done to avoid this situation? *

o.t: Initiated requirements planning to analyze, document, and manage requirements.
Applied requirements elicitation to involve engaging stakeholders consistently in the requirements process.
Implemented the change request process to harness change to the stakeholders’ advantage.
Used progressive elaboration to enhance the scope management plan with additional details.

questions.e: Applied requirements elicitation involves consistently engaging stakeholders to gather and clarify their needs. By doing so regularly and iteratively, the project manager ensures that requirements are well understood, avoids conflicting inputs, and keeps stakeholders aligned. This approach helps reduce confusion, build trust, and prevent scope creep, leading to a smoother project execution.

questions.q: In a multinational multi-location project with virtual teams a project manager has established a project baseline. The project manager discovers that multiple risk elements have appeared. The project manager did not foresee these risks during the planning stage of the project. What should the project manager calculate to address this critical budgetary situation? (Choose two) *

o.t: Contingency control in the project and rebaseline.
Mitigation control in the project.
Benefits management control in the project.
Integrated change control in the project.
Currency exchange rate.

questions.e: A. Contingency control in the project and rebaseline: Calculating and implementing contingency control helps to address unforeseen risks by allocating additional resources or time. Rebaselining the project ensures that the project plan reflects the updated scope, schedule, and budget considering the new risks. D. Integrated change control in the project: Integrated change control involves evaluating and managing changes to the project scope, schedule, and costs. This process ensures that any adjustments due to new risks are properly assessed, approved, and documented, maintaining project alignment with objectives.

questions.q: A project is in the knowledge transfer phase, and a few subject matter experts (SMEs) went to the client site for knowledge transfer. The SMEs captured various process deviations without sharing with the project team. How can the project manager ensure knowledge transfer across the team? *

o.t: Ask the project team to run a deviation log review meeting with the client, highlighting that the project may not be able to go live as scheduled.
Ask the project management office (PMO) to provide team members with real-time visibility for deviations and facilitate team members to resolve issues.
Ask the SMEs to share the knowledge transfer documents with all other members by placing the documents in the project management information system (PMIS).
Ask the project team to facilitate a lessons learned session during the project closure phase to incorporate this issue.

questions.e: Asking the SMEs to share the knowledge transfer documents with all other members by placing the documents in the PMIS ensures that all team members have access to the captured knowledge and process deviations. This promotes transparency, facilitates effective knowledge transfer, and helps the entire team stay informed and aligned.

questions.q: In an attempt to streamline project communications, a project manager established a shared portal for all stakeholders to get project information. The sponsor complained about this system and says that it is ineffective. What should the project manager have done to prevent this situation from occurring? *

o.t: Analyzed the sponsor's communication requirements.
Confirmed that the portal is providing adequate information.
Verified that the project team is following the communications management plan.
Ensured the sponsor had the necessary skills to use the portal.

questions.e: Analyzing the sponsor's communication requirements would have helped the project manager understand the sponsor's specific needs and preferences regarding project information. This would ensure that the chosen communication method aligns with the sponsor's expectations and prevents dissatisfaction with the communication system.

questions.q: A project manager is leading a meeting with key stakeholders, the project sponsor and the product owner to define the features that will be released after the next iteration. The purpose of the meeting is to review the product backlog prioritization, considering that during the past iteration some deliverables were not completed. Which two items should be taken into account first to review and update the product backlog priorities during the meeting? (Choose two) *

o.t: Complexity and the cost of development.
Industry trends and the technical approach.
Cost of delaying some features against business value.
Reusing components from another product.
Length of time each feature has been on the backlog.

questions.e: A. Complexity and the cost of development: Considering the complexity and cost helps in planning and resource allocation, ensuring that the team can realistically complete the prioritized features within the iteration's timeframe. C. Cost of delaying some features against business value: This is critical because it helps prioritize features that will deliver the highest value to the business if completed sooner, taking into account the impact of delays.

questions.q: The marketing team is moving from predictive to hybrid approaches for their projects. The marketing director is not familiar with hybrid approaches and does not support the new direction. What should the project manager do?

o.t: Advise the marketing director to receive formal training.
Ask the marketing team members to coach their director.
Train the marketing team and keep their director informed.
Mentor the marketing director on the approaches.

questions.e: Mentoring the marketing director on hybrid approaches allows for a personalized and supportive method of addressing their concerns and increasing their understanding of the new direction. This approach helps to build trust and buy-in from the director, facilitating a smoother transition to hybrid methodologies.

questions.q: A project manager works for a large software development company that has multiple strategic business groups. The project manager has been assigned to develop maintenance planning software for a power plant. The project manager heard that a similar project that was executed by another business group in the company recently failed. The project manager is concerned about the project's performance and wants to take steps to help the project succeed. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Evaluate the project risk and try to replace the project with another one within the organization.
Inform the project sponsor about the risk and try to convince them to withdraw the project.
Study and apply the lessons learned from the failed project so that this project does not follow the same pattern.
Continue executing the project using the project manager's usual methods as all projects are unique.

questions.e: Lessons learned are an essential part of project management. By studying and applying lessons from previous similar projects, the project manager can identify potential risks, issues, and areas for improvement. This proactive approach helps in avoiding the same pitfalls and increases the chances of project success. Simply continuing with usual methods (option D) or trying to replace or withdraw the project (options A and B) are not constructive solutions and do not address the underlying issues that led to the previous project's failure.

questions.q: The customer wants to show their stakeholders a tangible outcome faster. This requires advancing a milestone. Which two things should the project manager do? (Choose two)

o.t: Inform the customer that moving the milestone has a very high impact on project cost.
Escalate the Issue to senior management so they can impose a solution on the customer.
Convince the customer to keep the requirements as is and not move the milestone.
Review the customer's priorities regarding the desired requirements for the milestones.
Discuss which requirements can be delivered faster with the project team.

questions.e: When a customer wants to advance a milestone, it's important for the project manager to understand the customer's priorities and see which requirements are most critical. Reviewing the customer's priorities (option D) helps in aligning the project's focus with the customer's expectations. Discussing with the project team (option E) helps in determining which requirements can be delivered more quickly, enabling a feasible plan to meet the new milestone without significantly compromising on quality or increasing costs. Options A, B, and C are either not constructive or do not directly address the customer's request in a collaborative manner.

questions.q: A team is holding the first demonstration of the software built to date on a medium-sized project. The product owner has uncovered a number of issues they would like to be addressed before providing approval. How should the project manager approach this problem? *

o.t: Plan to address the issues through backlog grooming and incorporate them into the next sprint.
Refer the product owner to the change management plan, then escalate to the steering committee.
Refer the product owner to the signed business requirement document and explain that the current plan cannot facilitate these changes.
Tell the product owner the issues will be addressed in the second version of the software.

questions.e: In Agile projects, issues and changes are often addressed through backlog grooming, where the product owner and team review and prioritize the product backlog. By incorporating the issues into the next sprint, the project manager ensures that the feedback is considered and the product evolves to meet the product owner's expectations. Referring to change management plans or business requirement documents (options B and C) or deferring the issues to a future version (option D) may not be as responsive or collaborative, and could hinder the iterative improvement process central to Agile methodologies.

questions.q: A project manager is leading a product development project that requires high involvement from several stakeholders. What should the project manager do to ensure this involvement? *

o.t: Evaluate the engagement needs of stakeholders.
Distribute weekly status emails to stakeholders.
Engage the sponsor on the behavior of stakeholders.
Conduct weekly update meetings with stakeholders.

questions.e: To ensure high involvement from several stakeholders, the project manager should first evaluate the engagement needs of stakeholders (option A). This involves understanding how each stakeholder prefers to be engaged, their interests, influence, and the best methods for communication and involvement. Once the needs are understood, the project manager can tailor their engagement approach accordingly. While distributing weekly status emails (option B) and conducting weekly update meetings (option D) are practical steps, they are more tactical and do not address the fundamental need to understand and evaluate stakeholder engagement requirements. Engaging the sponsor on stakeholder behavior (option C) might be useful, but it is not the primary step for ensuring effective stakeholder involvement.

questions.q: A project needs to be outlined as a phased approach for multiple product lines with a review gate at the end of each phase. To ensure consistency for this hybrid delivery, what should the project manager do? *

o.t: Ask subject matter experts (SMEs) to provide a detailed plan for each phase.
Commit to a detailed global plan from the initiation phase.
Get agreement from stakeholders on high-level deliverables and requirements.
Request the project management office (PMO) to review the initial plan

questions.e: For a phased approach with review gates, it is crucial to have stakeholder agreement on high-level deliverables and requirements (option C). This ensures that everyone has a clear understanding of what needs to be achieved at each phase, and it provides a framework for consistency throughout the project's lifecycle. This high-level agreement helps align expectations and provides a basis for more detailed planning and adjustments as the project progresses. Asking SMEs for detailed plans (option A) or committing to a detailed global plan from the initiation phase (option B) may be premature and lack flexibility. Involving the PMO to review the initial plan (option D) can be useful, but it should follow stakeholder alignment on the project's high-level deliverables and requirements.

questions.q: Which two actions should a project manager consider while launching a new virtual team? (Choose two) *

o.t: Recruit the best resources within the organization to be part of the virtual team.
Evaluate the project manager’s own strengths and weaknesses as a virtual team leader to identify avoidable pitfalls.
Identify the types and quantities of resources required for each work package or activity.
Establish in the beginning, how progress will be monitored and the best means for communicating progress.
Verify if team members are on more than one team and cannot devote enough time to this team.

questions.e: B. Evaluate the project manager’s own strengths and weaknesses as a virtual team leader to identify avoidable pitfalls: Self-awareness as a leader is crucial in a virtual environment. Understanding one's own strengths and weaknesses helps the project manager to better manage and lead the team, addressing any potential leadership gaps early on. D. Establish in the beginning, how progress will be monitored and the best means for communicating progress: Clear communication and progress monitoring are essential in a virtual team. Establishing these mechanisms at the start ensures that team members are aligned, know what is expected of them, and how their progress will be tracked and reported, which helps in maintaining productivity and accountability.

questions.q: A company that is heavily focused on delivering projects using predictive approaches on-boards a new project manager who uses hybrid approaches. The scope of the project contains a number of unclear requirements. How should the project manager plan the delivery of the project? *

o.t: Wait for the requirements to be more clear before any further action is taken on the project.
Ignore the unclear requirements and focus on the delivery plan of the project.
Escalate the issue of unclear requirements to the management team and wait for final authorization.
Break down the requirements and prioritize the requirements into iterative work packages.

questions.e: When dealing with unclear requirements in a project, especially when using a hybrid approach, it's effective to break down the requirements and prioritize them into iterative work packages (option D). This allows for parts of the project to move forward while gradually clarifying and refining the unclear requirements. This approach balances the predictive and adaptive methods, enabling the team to make progress while managing uncertainty. Waiting for the requirements to be completely clear (option A) can cause unnecessary delays, ignoring the unclear requirements (option B) is impractical, and escalating the issue (option C) without taking proactive steps can lead to stagnation.

questions.q: An integrated project involves the interaction of both hardware and software and the sponsor has approved the schedule management plan. The project team evaluated the product's feasibility of functionality and accelerated testing. What should the project manager do as a servant leader? *

o.t: Support the team as necessary to find the minimum viable product (MVP).
Amend the project budget to include MVP testing.
Submit a change request to the project sponsor for accelerated testing.
Develop the product as per the schedule to perform integration and testing.

questions.e: As a servant leader, the project manager's role is to support the team in achieving their goals and removing any obstacles that may hinder their progress. Supporting the team in finding the minimum viable product (MVP) (option A) aligns with the principles of servant leadership by focusing on delivering value early and often. This approach also allows for feedback and iterative improvement, which is crucial for integrated projects involving both hardware and software. Amending the budget (option B) and submitting a change request (option C) are more administrative actions and may not directly address the team's immediate needs. Developing the product strictly according to the schedule (option D) without considering the need for an MVP might overlook opportunities for early validation and adjustment.

questions.q: A team has different ideas on how to address a feature of a product under construction and; although the sprint began two days ago, they have still not reached a consensus. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Ask the product owner, who is the key stakeholder, to choose among the different ideas.
Propose ideas to the group, ask everyone to vote, and then choose the most popular idea.
Schedule a session to give everyone the chance to express their opinions about each idea, then vote and decide.
Offer an opinion about the pros and cons of each idea and try to reach a consensus in a facilitated meeting.

questions.e: When a team is struggling to reach a consensus, it's important to create an environment where everyone's opinions are heard and considered. By scheduling a session for team members to express their opinions about each idea and then voting (option C), the project manager facilitates a democratic process that can help the team reach a decision collectively. This approach ensures that all perspectives are taken into account, fostering team collaboration and ownership of the decision. Asking the product owner to choose (option A) may undermine team autonomy, and proposing ideas and voting without discussion (option B) may not fully explore the merits of each idea. Offering an opinion and trying to reach a consensus in a facilitated meeting (option D) is also a viable approach, but ensuring that the team has an opportunity to discuss and vote might be more inclusive and effective in this context.

questions.q: A project manager has joined a company m an unfamiliar industry and has been given a strategically important project Being new, and not fully understanding the interdependences of the various departmental work items, the project manager is unsure of how to plan the project How should the project manager proceed? *

o.t: Consult the project sponsor and request their feedback.
Consult the product owner and request a complete prioritization session.
Consult a senior project manager within the organization and request their expert judgement.
Consult a senior developer within the organization and request their input.

questions.e: When a project manager is new to a company and industry, seeking guidance from a senior project manager within the organization (option C) is a prudent step. Senior project managers typically have a broad understanding of the organization's processes, interdependencies, and best practices. Their expert judgment can provide valuable insights into planning and managing the project effectively. While consulting the project sponsor (option A) or product owner (option B) can also provide useful information, a senior project manager is more likely to offer comprehensive guidance on project management practices. Consulting a senior developer (option D) may help with technical aspects but may not cover broader project management interdependencies and planning needs.

questions.q: In the beginning of project execution, the project manager finds out that a key resource will be unavailable for two weeks which could cause a delay to the schedule. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Assign the tasks to another resource, and ask the resource to work double shifts.
Update the schedule to reflect the project's changes in duration.
Ask human resources (HR) for a replacement, and update the risk register.
Update the resource management plan and resource allocation chart accordingly.

questions.e: The first step a project manager should take when discovering a key resource will be unavailable is to update the resource management plan and resource allocation chart (option D). This ensures that the project documentation accurately reflects the current state of resource availability, allowing for better planning and adjustment of tasks. Once this is done, the project manager can then explore options for mitigating the impact, such as reassigning tasks, adjusting the schedule, or seeking additional resources if necessary. Assigning tasks to another resource without proper planning (option A) or immediately updating the schedule (option B) might not consider the overall project impact and dependencies. Requesting a replacement from HR (option C) is a potential action but should come after the resource management plan is updated and a thorough assessment of the situation is conducted.

questions.q: A project manager accepts a delivery at the project site but the items are of a poor quality. The project manager gets the local vendor to fix the items but more deliveries from this vendor are expected. What should the project manager do going forward? *

o.t: Allocate extra time to inspect deliveries for quality assurance upon arrival at the site.
Review the contract requirements and ask for the applicable evidence for quality assurance.
Have the vendor issue the quality documentation prior to the next delivery.
Call the vendor and have them verbally guarantee the quality of the next site delivery.

questions.e: Reviewing the contract requirements and requesting applicable evidence for quality assurance ensures that the vendor complies with the agreed-upon quality standards. This formal approach helps prevent future quality issues by holding the vendor accountable to the contract terms and providing documented assurance of quality.

questions.q: A new team member is hired and the training is taking longer than expected. This impacts the overall project performance. What immediate action should the project manager take to improve the situation? *

o.t: Communicate this issue to the human resources department.
Provide additional training to the new hire.
Increase team cohesiveness by sharing information and experiences openly.
Update the issue log and define the mitigation strategy.

questions.e: Updating the issue log and defining the mitigation strategy is the immediate action the project manager should take. This ensures that the issue is formally documented, and a clear plan is established to address and mitigate the impact on project performance. While providing additional training (option B) or increasing team cohesiveness (option C) might be part of the mitigation strategy, they are actions that follow after the issue is logged and a strategy is outlined. Communicating the issue to the human resources department (option A) might be necessary but is not the first step in resolving the immediate impact on the project.

questions.q: The team architect resigned from the company. The new architect points out a design flaw during a planning meeting that may potentially impact the final quality. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Review the scope management plan.
Update the design with changes.
Request an architecture review.
Update the quality management plan.

questions.e: When a new architect identifies a potential design flaw that could impact the final quality, the first step should be to request an architecture review (option C). This review will help thoroughly assess the flaw, determine its implications, and explore potential solutions. This approach ensures that the issue is properly evaluated before any changes are made to the design or project plans. Reviewing the scope management plan (option A), updating the design (option B), or updating the quality management plan (option D) might be necessary steps following the review, depending on the findings and recommendations.

questions.q: In an industrial plant, the owner has decided to add more capacity to the plant by installing a new machine and updating the software used in production. This capacity enlargement will occur while the plant is still functioning and producing. The software update will be accomplished using an agile approach in order to minimize risk. The machine procurement, installation, and integration will be accomplished using predictive approaches What types of communications will the project manager have to design into the schedule management plan to ensure the project will be on schedule? *

o.t: Weekly colocated meetings with the relevant stakeholders.
Biweekly conference calls with the relevant stakeholders.
Weekly one-on-one meetings with each of the relevant stakeholders.
Biweekly written status reports from the relevant stakeholders.

questions.e: Biweekly conference calls with relevant stakeholders (option B) provide a balanced approach to ensure regular and effective communication while keeping the project on schedule. This method allows for timely updates, discussions, and problem-solving, which is crucial when managing a project that involves both predictive and agile approaches. Weekly colocated meetings (option A) may not be practical or necessary, especially in a functioning industrial plant. Weekly one-on-one meetings (option C) could be time-consuming and less efficient for overall coordination. Biweekly written status reports (option D) provide updates but lack the immediacy and interactivity of conference calls, which are important for dynamic project environments.

questions.q: A project manager is managing an innovation project for a big corporation. The project manager is planning to use email as the main communication channel, however, the product owner prefers to use another approved communication tool instead of email. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Contact the sponsor to request direction regarding the communication tool to be used by the project team.
Update the communications management plan based on the product owner’s preferences and distribute to the team.
Suggest to the team to start using the communication tool suggested by the product owner.
Request the product owner to use email because using another tool will increase the workload.

questions.e: The project manager should update the communications management plan based on the product owner’s preferences and distribute it to the team (option B). This ensures that the communication plan is aligned with stakeholder preferences and promotes effective communication. Effective communication is crucial for project success, and accommodating the product owner's preferred tool can improve collaboration and stakeholder satisfaction. Consulting the sponsor (option A) or requesting the product owner to use email (option D) may not address the underlying preference issue directly, and simply suggesting the team use the tool without updating the plan (option C) could lead to inconsistency in communication practices.

questions.q: A new team member inquires about how much they need to learn about the organizational process assets (OPAs) residing on the company intranet. Another team member states they only need to know the basics. However, the project manager believes the team member should know everything regarding the OPAs. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Create a training schedule for the new team member to follow over the next few weeks.
Escalate the inquiry to the team member's functional manager.
Clarify the relevance of reviewing the documentation on the intranet.
Ask a senior team member to help the new team member navigate through all the documentation.

questions.e: The project manager should clarify the relevance of reviewing the documentation on the intranet (option C). By explaining the importance of the organizational process assets (OPAs) and how they impact the project, the project manager can ensure that the new team member understands why it is essential to be familiar with them. This approach helps in highlighting the critical aspects of OPAs that are necessary for their role, without overwhelming them with unnecessary details. Creating a training schedule (option A) or asking a senior team member to help (option D) may be useful follow-up actions, but the immediate step should be to clarify the relevance first. Escalating the inquiry (option B) is not necessary and may complicate the situation.

questions.q: In the middle of a project, a business unit manager who regularly interacts with the project manager's team is promoted to a higher management position. The replacement manager is from the same unit and is somewhat familiar with the project. After getting more information about the new manager, what is the project manager's next step? *

o.t: Contact the previous business unit manager to learn more about the new manager.
Update the stakeholder register and the stakeholder engagement plan to include the new manager.
Send the new manager a copy of the project charter to ensure the project objectives are understood.
Schedule a meeting with the new manager to discuss the business analysis team's plans.

questions.e: The project manager should update the stakeholder register and the stakeholder engagement plan to include the new manager (option B). This step ensures that the new manager is formally recognized as a stakeholder, and their engagement and communication preferences are documented. This will help in maintaining effective communication and stakeholder management throughout the project. While scheduling a meeting with the new manager (option D) and ensuring they understand the project objectives (option C) are important subsequent steps, updating the stakeholder documentation is the immediate priority to keep project records accurate and up-to-date. Contacting the previous manager (option A) might provide additional insights but is not the primary step in updating stakeholder management processes.

questions.q: From previous lessons learned working with a client, a project manager notes that the client's turn-around times on documents sent for approval were very slow and well outside of the agreed timelines. At the initial kick-off meeting with the same client, how should the project manager approach this issue for the new project? *

o.t: Inform the client that extra resources will be added to give the client more time for reviews.
Update the project risk register with the potential for delays.
Work with the client on an acceptable amount of time for document approval.
Inform the client of their responsibility in relation to document approval.

questions.e: At the initial kick-off meeting, it's crucial to address any potential issues proactively. By working with the client to establish an acceptable amount of time for document approval (option C), the project manager sets clear expectations and agreements that can help mitigate delays. This collaborative approach helps ensure that both parties are aligned and can work together more effectively. Simply informing the client of their responsibility (option D) or adding extra resources (option A) does not directly address the root cause of the delays. Updating the risk register (option B) is important but should be done after discussing and agreeing on acceptable timelines with the client.

questions.q: A project manager is working on a large project with a very difficult client. During the course of the project, the project manager realizes that if the project team had a little more time and funding to make some minor changes, the client could realize the benefits of 25% of the project outcomes early. How should the project manager approach this? *

o.t: Concentrate on the current project milestones.
Update the project management plan for this new work.
Develop a business case and submit it to the client.
Make all the changes and then show the client the results.

questions.e: When a project manager identifies an opportunity to deliver a significant portion of project benefits early, the appropriate approach is to develop a business case (option C). This business case should detail the additional time and funding required, the changes to be made, and the anticipated early benefits. Submitting this to the client provides a formal proposal for consideration and ensures that the client can make an informed decision based on the potential value. Concentrating only on current milestones (option A) or making changes without approval (option D) might overlook the potential benefits and could lead to scope creep. Updating the project management plan (option B) should occur after the client has approved the business case.

questions.q: During an ongoing project a key resource asks the project manager about the project purpose and if it is aligned with the organization's strategy. What should the project manager share with the key resource? *

o.t: The updated benefits management plan.
The updated scope management plan.
The updated project management plan.
The updated communications management plan.

questions.e: The benefits management plan outlines the project’s purpose and its alignment with the organization's strategy, including the expected benefits and how they contribute to the strategic goals. Sharing the updated benefits management plan (option A) with the key resource provides clear information on the project's objectives, expected outcomes, and how it aligns with the broader organizational strategy. The scope management plan (option B), project management plan (option C), and communications management plan (option D) contain important information, but they do not specifically address the project's purpose and strategic alignment as directly as the benefits management plan does.

questions.q: A project team member was unhappy with a new change in project governance and complained to one of the project sponsors. The project sponsor challenged the project manager. How should the project manager resolve this conflict? *

o.t: Arrange a meeting with the project team member and project sponsor to discuss the change and obtain consensus.
Discuss how to manage this conflict with the project management office (PMO) and let them decide how to resolve the issue.
Explain to the sponsor why the change is required and get their support in forcing the project team member to accept the new change.
Schedule a meeting with the project team member's functional manager and request the functional manager's support.

questions.e: In situations where there is a conflict regarding project governance, it is important for the project manager to facilitate a discussion between the parties involved. Arranging a meeting with the project team member and the project sponsor to discuss the concerns and work towards a consensus is a proactive approach. This allows for open communication, ensures that all viewpoints are heard, and works towards a collaborative solution. It aligns with conflict resolution techniques that emphasize problem-solving and collaboration.

questions.q: A project manager is managing a project to develop a new tool. Because of the nature of the project, the project manager decides to use an agile approach. One of the identified risks becomes an issue when the project manager finds out that another company patented a very similar tool. What should the project manager do to address this issued? *

o.t: Schedule a meeting with critical stakeholders to review the issue and decide on the next steps.
Put the project on hold and release the resources until the issue is resolved.
Inform the product owner and log the issue in the risk register to monitor closely for next steps.
Contact the company that owns the patent of the similar tool to compare the similarities and differences with the current project.

questions.e: When an identified risk becomes an issue, it is essential to address it promptly and collaboratively. Scheduling a meeting with critical stakeholders (option A) allows the project manager to gather input, discuss the implications of the patent issue, and collectively decide on the best course of action. This approach ensures that all key parties are informed and involved in the decision-making process, which is crucial for resolving significant issues effectively. Putting the project on hold (option B) is a drastic measure and should be considered only after exploring all possible solutions. Informing the product owner and logging the issue in the risk register (option C) is important but insufficient as an immediate action. Contacting the company that owns the patent (option D) may be part of the steps decided upon during the stakeholders' meeting, but it is not the first step to take.

questions.q: The project manager has finished all the tasks of the project and immediately starts on a new project. A few months after beginning the new project, the accounting manager asks for confirmation of previous projects because the budget is still open with no further cash flows. What should the project manager have done? *

o.t: Conveyed task completion information to accounting.
Closed the procurement process properly.
Completed the transition process.
Performed administrative closure of the project.

questions.e: Administrative closure involves finalizing all project activities, including ensuring all contracts are closed, confirming all deliverables have been completed, and that all project documentation is properly archived. This step ensures that the project is officially closed and that all financials are reconciled, preventing situations where budgets remain open with no further cash flows.

questions.q: An events company is planning their annual event for a retirement fund. The organization has run the event planning using agile approaches for the last 3 years. During the initiation phase, while assessing possible risks and improvements for the event, the project manager uses previous event feedback to assist in developing the risk register. Which ceremony should be used in developing this register? *

o.t: Sprint plan.
Retrospective results.
Sprint report.
Project status report.

questions.e: Retrospectives review past iterations to gather feedback on what went well, what didn't, and what could be improved. This feedback is crucial for identifying potential risks and developing the risk register, particularly during the initiation phase when historical data is valuable for planning and risk management.

questions.q: A project manager has been appointed to a multimillion-dollar project. The project is considered to be high risk since no similar projects have been undertaken before and there is no historical data Some external stakeholders are reluctant to provide support. What approach should the project manager take? *

o.t: Examine the plans, processes, policies, and knowledge that are specific to the organization undertaking the project.
Establish dialogue with stakeholders on the project constraints, assumptions, and critical inputs.
Convince senior management to close the project since the project lacks sponsorship and is considered to be high risk.
Host a project team meeting, then update the risk register and the project management plan.

questions.e: For a high-risk project with reluctant stakeholders and no historical data, it's essential to engage stakeholders early and establish a clear understanding of the project's constraints, assumptions, and critical inputs. This helps in building trust, gaining their support, and ensuring that all potential risks are identified and managed effectively. Open communication with stakeholders is crucial in navigating uncertainties and securing the necessary backing for the project's success.

questions.q: During the execution phase of a project a new project manager is assigned to replace the previous project manager. As the project manager starts managing the project, they discover that team performance is significantly decreasing, which is impacting the project's key performance indicators (KPIs). This team has delivered good performance on similar projects in the past What should the project manager do next to improve this situation? *

o.t: Call for a team meeting to identify the root cause for the declining performance.
Estimate the baseline impacts and submit a change request.
Implement compression techniques to bring the project back on track.
Review the resource management plan and organizational assets.

questions.e: When team performance is declining, it's crucial to understand the underlying reasons before taking any corrective actions. Calling a team meeting to identify the root cause helps gather insights directly from the team members, who may provide valuable information about what is affecting their performance. Once the root cause is identified, appropriate measures can be taken to address the issues and improve performance.

questions.q: A project manager is leading a large-scale project that involves 70 stakeholders. The project manager has heard various comments and expectations from the customers, some of which are contradictory Consequently, some requirements are not clear. What should the project manager do to build consensus regarding the requirements? *

o.t: Escalate the issue to the management team for their review and guidance.
Create a survey template to collect feedback from stakeholders to reach an agreement.
Organize a face-to-face meeting with all stakeholders to understand their interests and concerns.
Leverage expert judgment to determine the requirements that should be considered.

questions.e: Organizing a face-to-face meeting with all stakeholders is an effective way to understand their interests and concerns directly. It provides an opportunity for open communication, allowing stakeholders to express their views and resolve any contradictory requirements. This approach helps in building consensus and ensuring that all stakeholders are aligned on the project's requirements.

questions.q: A regulatory branch of an environmental government agency has recently placed a ban on the manufacturing of a specified thickness of plastic packaging products. This ban will take effect in 12 months. The project manager for a startup firm working in alternative packaging has been monitoring the progress of this law for a while and as part of the risk management, has identified new products that can support a growing customer base. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Continue production processes and plan to discuss changes at the next annual target review meeting.
Begin a marketing campaign to sell alternative packaging after the 12-month period ends.
Inform management of the new law as an opportunity to expand market share and share the proposed products.
Organize a meeting with all stakeholders and review the stakeholder engagement plan.

questions.e: Informing management about the new law and presenting it as an opportunity to expand market share with the proposed alternative products is a proactive approach. It allows the project manager to align the company's strategy with regulatory changes and leverage the new products to capture a growing customer base. This step ensures that management is aware of the impending change and can make informed decisions about the company's direction.

questions.q: In the middle of a project incremental delivery, due to a change in the techn ology, a team member informed the project leader that due to a lack of knowledge in the technology the delivery will be delayed and suggests outsourcing services. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Inform the end user of the delay of the specific delivery due to the new technology
Search for an outsourcing service with the experience needed
Inform the sponsor of the delay and ask for their support and approval
Discuss the impact of the new technology with the team and decide action jointly

questions.e: When faced with a technology change that impacts delivery, it's essential to understand the implications thoroughly and collaborate with the team to determine the best course of action. Discussing the impact with the team allows for a collective evaluation of potential solutions, including whether outsourcing is necessary or if there are other ways to address the knowledge gap. This approach ensures that the decision is well-informed and considers the perspectives of those directly involved in the project.

questions.q: The project manager is experiencing delays with two critical tasks that are to be executed by two different teams. The project manager realizes that the functional managers of these two teams have an unsolved conflict and they are not communicating properly. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Arrange a meeting with the managers and try to reach an agreement.
Communicate with the project sponsor regarding the need to resolve the conflict between the managers.
Evaluate the impact of the delay on the project and look for alternatives to create a remediation plan.
Meet with both teams and their managers and try to figure out the root cause of the conflict.

questions.e: Meeting with both teams and their managers to understand the root cause of the conflict is a crucial step. This allows the project manager to address the underlying issues directly, facilitating better communication and collaboration between the teams. Understanding the root cause will help in finding a sustainable resolution and improving the coordination necessary for the project's success.

questions.q: A project manager is working with an agile team. A key stakeholder who does not join the sprint planning session is very unhappy, as the delivery date for the final product has been pushed back three times. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Meet with the stakeholder to understand the concern and business impact, reprioritize as necessary, and invite them to join the sprint planning session.
Direct the product owner to drop other work in progress and work on this stakeholder’s requirement as the top-priority item.
Share the prioritized items that the team is working on with the stakeholder and invite them to join the sprint planning session.
Secure some additional funding to recruit more resources to the project team to enable faster delivery.

questions.e: Meeting with the stakeholder to understand their concerns and the business impact of the delays is essential. This approach helps in addressing the stakeholder's dissatisfaction and allows for a discussion on how to potentially reprioritize work to better align with their expectations. Inviting the stakeholder to the sprint planning session ensures they are involved in the planning process, which can lead to better alignment and communication moving forward.

questions.q: A vendor informed the project manager that a critical resource will be on a long leave of absence. The project team reviewed the pending vendor deliverables and identified an alternative solution, but the solution will incur an additional cost. The project is currently on schedule and slightly under budget. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Request a replacement resource.
Perform a cost-benefit analysis.
Implement risk responses.
Perform Integrated Change Control.

questions.e: When the project team identifies an alternative solution that incurs additional costs, this constitutes a change to the project scope, schedule, or budget. Integrated Change Control is the process of reviewing, approving, and managing changes to the project. The project manager needs to follow this process to formally evaluate and approve the change, ensuring that the impact on the project is understood and documented, and that the change is properly communicated to stakeholders. This step helps maintain control over the project's direction and ensures alignment with overall goals.

questions.q: A labor union contract negotiation is delaying the completion of a project to build a new manufacturing plant. Because the labor contract was due for renewal this year, the project manager documented the negotiation process as a risk to the project. The project was about to start the first phase of equipment installation at the plant when the negotiation began. How should the project manager address the situation? *

o.t: Meet with the project team to determine options for risk mitigation.
Log the issue and follow the planned actions in the risk response plan.
Acquire contract resources and submit a change request for the cost impact.
Escalate the issue to the steering committee to ask for mitigation support.

questions.e: Since the project manager had already documented the labor contract negotiation process as a risk, there should be a risk response plan in place. Logging the issue and following the planned actions in the risk response plan ensures that the team addresses the situation systematically and according to the pre-determined strategy. This approach helps in managing the risk effectively and keeps the project aligned with its risk management processes.

questions.q: A project manager is managing two agile teams and reviewing their metrics to find out which team is performing better. Which approach should be taken? *

o.t: The team with the higher velocity is performing better and should be rewarded.
The issue should be addressed as part of a retrospective in the next iteration.
The velocity should not be compared as teams can size items differently.
The velocity of both teams should be compared at the end of every iteration.

questions.e: In agile, velocity is a measure of the amount of work a team completes during a sprint. However, different teams may use different methods for estimating and sizing their work items, making direct comparisons of velocity between teams unreliable and potentially misleading. Instead of comparing velocities, it is better to focus on each team's continuous improvement and performance relative to their own past iterations.

questions.q: A project manager is leading a new agile project. The requirements for the first sprint have been defined and the work is about to start. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Assign the tasks to the resources based on their expertise.
Ensure that the priority of each task is clear to the team.
Ask the team to self-organize and manage the work assigned.
Tell the team which task to focus on at the next daily standup.

questions.e: In agile project management, particularly with Scrum, the team is expected to be self-organizing. This means that the team members decide how best to accomplish the work within the sprint, including who will work on which tasks. Encouraging the team to self-organize fosters ownership, accountability, and collaboration, which are core principles of agile methodologies.

questions.q: The project manager is reviewing the program risks and issues with key stakeholders One of the stakeholders wants to understand when the risk may potentially become an issue. What artifact should the project manager share with the stakeholder? *

o.t: Issue log.
Project management plan.
Risk management plan.
Risk register.

questions.e: The risk register is the artifact that documents all identified risks, their analysis, response plans, and the risk status. It includes information about the potential impact and timing of risks, which can help stakeholders understand when a risk might materialize into an issue. Sharing the risk register with the stakeholder will provide the necessary insights into the timing and potential impact of risks.

questions.q: A project manager is assigned to a new project. The project management office (PMO) and the project manager agree that this is the right opportunity to include daily standup meetings. The project team has never used such tools, and a few members are challenging the decision. What should the project manager do in this situation? *

o.t: Engage an external vendor to perform the design phase under an iterative approach.
Request that new team members familiar with iterative approaches be assigned to this project.
Update the project schedule to consider a daily standup as part of the project design phase.
Define the ground rules, responsibilities, and conflict management strategies.

questions.e: When introducing new practices such as daily standup meetings, it's important to set clear expectations and guidelines. Defining ground rules, responsibilities, and conflict management strategies helps the team understand the purpose and structure of the standups, and how to address any concerns or challenges. This approach fosters a smoother transition to the new practice and promotes a collaborative team environment.

questions.q: During the review of a project's list of deliverables, one of the stakeholders expressed concern that one of the requirements will not be addressed. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Check the approved list of requirements to see if there are any missing items.
Work with the stakeholder to improve the requirements' acceptance criteria.
Review the requirements traceability matrix with the concerned stakeholder.
Discuss with the stakeholder which additional requirements should be added.

questions.e: The requirements traceability matrix (RTM) links requirements to their corresponding deliverables, ensuring that all requirements are addressed throughout the project lifecycle. By reviewing the RTM with the concerned stakeholder, the project manager can verify whether the requirement in question has been captured and trace its progress. This helps in clarifying any misunderstandings and ensuring that all requirements are properly managed.

questions.q: The rollout of a new finance system is in the execution phase. A number of issues have surfaced in the last month that are slowing the project down A new project sponsor has recently started with the company but has not had time to meet the project manager. The project is at the point where the issues are significantly impacting delivery of the project. How should the project manager alert the new project sponsor about these concerns? *

o.t: Send an email invitation to the project sponsor to attend all of the project team's weekly meetings, and hope the sponsor will find time to attend.
Send an email to the project sponsor summarizing the project status and key concerns, and request an immediate face-to-face meeting to discuss them.
Continue emailing updated project status reports highlighting the key risks and issues, and wait for the project sponsor to request a meeting.
Complete a risk analysis outlining the delays and impacts, and email a copy of the risk register, urging the project sponsor to respond.

questions.e: Sending an email summarizing the project status and key concerns and requesting an immediate face-to-face meeting ensures that the new project sponsor is quickly brought up to speed on the critical issues impacting the project. This approach facilitates direct communication and allows for a more effective discussion of the concerns, enabling timely decision-making and support from the sponsor.

questions.q: A company's project management office (PMO) has started to implement iterative tools A project manager is starting a new project and has identified an opportunity to use the iterative tools One of the senior managers is concerned about this modified framework as it is fairly new to the company. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Organize individual sessions with the stakeholders to build awareness and trust in the new framework.
Look for external training on the new framework to eliminate the risk of low engagement from stakeholders.
Send documentation to the senior manager about the advantages of the new framework.
Escalate the senior manager's concern to the project sponsor and distribute the status to the team.

questions.e: Organizing individual sessions with stakeholders to build awareness and trust in the new framework is a proactive approach. It allows the project manager to address concerns, provide education on the benefits and workings of the new iterative tools, and foster a supportive environment for the change. This approach helps in gaining stakeholder buy-in and ensures smoother implementation of the new framework.

questions.q: A team is assembled for a new project that will be using a predictive approach through requirements gathering and an agile approach for development and testing. Not everyone on the team has experience working in agile. The schedule has started slipping due to the unclear structure of the agile development approach. What should the project manager have done to avoid this situation? *

o.t: Established daily standup meetings to track and report on team progress and escalated delays to stakeholders as they occurred.
Set up weekly status meetings to review team progress, prepared weekly status reports to track progress and regularly escalated delays.
Met with the team, allowed team members to make decisions about what to do and established performance goals.
Conducted routine meetings and identified team members who are under performing.

questions.e: Meeting with the team and allowing team members to make decisions about their work is a key principle of agile methodologies. Establishing clear performance goals helps ensure that everyone understands their responsibilities and the expectations for progress. This collaborative approach helps in clarifying the structure and processes of the agile development approach, which could have prevented the schedule from slipping.

questions.q: During a documentation audit of an international company, it was identified that the last version of the project schedule was from one month ago even though the project manager knew it was recently updated. How should the project manager have handled documentation for the project? *
