o.t: Updated the project management plan regularly and had it securely shared with all stakeholders.
Assigned a project team member to ensure all project documentation was updated.
Reviewed the risk register to identify a response plan for the audit.
Kept documentation in the project management information system (PMIS), and shared it with appropriate stakeholders.

questions.e: The project manager should have used a Project Management Information System (PMIS) to store and manage project documentation, including the project schedule. This ensures that all documents are consistently updated and accessible to the relevant stakeholders. By keeping the documentation in the PMIS, the project manager ensures that everyone has access to the most current version and that any updates are tracked, reducing the likelihood of outdated information being used.

questions.q: An organization has historically executed most projects using a predictive approach. The organization now wants to change over to an agile approach. Which strategy will be useful to effectively help prepare the organization for this change? *

o.t: Create a task force of executives who will monitor agile projects on a daily basis.
Add multiple layers of managers who will be accountable for the agile execution.
Improve organizational readiness by addressing impediments to agile in the organization.
Take a big bang approach of moving the whole organization to agile at once.

questions.e: Improving organizational readiness by addressing impediments to agile involves identifying and removing barriers that could hinder the successful adoption of agile practices. This strategy ensures a smoother transition by preparing the organization culturally and structurally for the change, fostering an environment that supports agile methodologies. It helps in gradually building the necessary skills, mindset, and processes needed for effective agile execution.

questions.q: A client is structured as a matrix organization for an agile project. The project manager is working on-site with key stakeholders from different parts of the organization. How should the project manager handle the different stakeholders? *

o.t: All stakeholders are important, so the project manager should follow directions provided by management and key stakeholders.
Because there are different perspectives perform a stakeholder analysis and act based on the outcome.
The project manager is working on the client's premises, so follow the directions of all the key stakeholders.
This is an agile project, so listen only to the directions of the project manager's supervisor and the functional managers of the organization.

questions.e: Performing a stakeholder analysis helps the project manager understand the different perspectives, interests, and levels of influence of the stakeholders. This analysis allows the project manager to prioritize and address the needs and concerns of the stakeholders effectively, ensuring that the project aligns with the overall objectives and expectations. Acting based on the outcome of the stakeholder analysis facilitates better communication, collaboration, and decision-making.

questions.q: A project manager learns from a marketing analyst that a competitor just published a press release announcing a product launch using a specific innovation. The project manager is concerned because the company is initiating a project involving the same innovation A key goal of the new project is that the product will be the first to market won the innovation. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Document the issue in the issue log and escalate to the project sponsor.
Inform the project sponsor and suggest canceling the project.
Review the project goals and eat criteria m the project charter.
Ask the leader of research and development to decide on next steps.

questions.e: When a significant issue arises that can impact the project goals, the project manager should first document the issue in the issue log. This ensures that the issue is formally recognized and tracked. Escalating to the project sponsor is appropriate because it allows the sponsor, who has the authority and responsibility for the project, to make decisions on how to address the issue, including potential changes to project scope, goals, or timelines.

questions.q: A team has been consistently delivering outcomes. However, based on their current performance, it was discovered that their velocity has decreased by 30%. What should the project manager do to ensure the velocity is under control? *

o.t: Ask the product owner to look at a minimum of four to eight iterations and replan the velocity for the next iteration based on the team's current performance.
Ask the scrum master to plug gaps in the team's performance by adding a team member to compensate for the velocity decrease.
Request that the team improve their cycle time to compensate for the velocity decrease.
Request the team to improve the lead time, cycle time, and response time individually and track closure.

questions.e: Velocity is an important metric in agile projects that helps teams understand their capacity and performance over time. A sudden decrease in velocity should be examined over multiple iterations to understand if it is a trend or an anomaly. The product owner, in collaboration with the team, should review past performance data (typically four to eight iterations) to replan and set realistic expectations for future iterations. This helps in understanding the root cause of the decrease and making informed decisions.

questions.q: A project manager scheduled a session to identify risks on the current project. Most of the stakeholders did not attend the meeting, although they previously confirmed their attendance. How should the project manager proceed in order to complete the risk register? *

o.t: Cancel the meeting and create the risk register using the project documents.
Continue the meeting and send the updated risk register to all stakeholders.
Run the meeting and follow up with each one of the absent stakeholders to get their input.
Escalate the issue of stakeholders not attending the meeting to the project sponsor.

questions.e: Continuing the meeting with available participants ensures that some risks are identified and the process moves forward. Following up individually with the absent stakeholders allows the project manager to gather additional risks and insights that were missed due to their absence. This ensures a comprehensive risk register and demonstrates proactive management without immediate escalation.

questions.q: A team has been working for two months and has consistently missed planned user stories. How should the project manager address this issue? *

o.t: Ensure the sprint size is appropriate for the iteration duration.
Promote changing the iteration duration in order to commit as planned.
Engage in recruiting a highly skilled resource to reinforce the skills.
Consider using a reward system to encourage timely delivery.

questions.e: Consistently missing planned user stories indicates that the team might be overcommitting or that the sprint size (the amount of work planned for the sprint) is not appropriate for the iteration duration. Ensuring that the sprint size matches the team's capacity and the iteration duration helps in setting realistic expectations and achievable goals, leading to more consistent delivery of user stories.

questions.q: Two key team members suggest different options to prevent time overruns and delays. There is a conflict between these two team members because of their divergent views. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Schedule a meeting between the team members to find a solution.
Refer the team members to the project charter to resolve the conflict.
Issue a new change request to evaluate this situation and communicate the result.
Document the facts explained by the team members in the issue log.

questions.e: Scheduling a meeting between the team members allows for a collaborative approach to resolving the conflict. It provides a platform for both parties to discuss their viewpoints, understand each other’s perspectives, and work together to find a mutually agreeable solution. This approach promotes teamwork and can lead to a better and more comprehensive solution to prevent time overruns and delays.

questions.q: The city has decided to build a new tram station. The project will include various approaches. The construction and infrastructure work will be accomplished using a predictive life cycle while software will be developed using an iterative life cycle. Some neighbors are resisting the project have been asking the mayor to stop the project, and are threatening legal action. What two actions should the project manager take? *

o.t: Discuss with the construction team alternatives on moving the new train station to another location.
Publish information on the city’s website about the benefits that the new tram station will bring.
Have a meeting with the mayor and explain the importance of the new train station to the city.
Conduct regular meetings with the neighbors to get their buy-in for the project.
Register this situation as a risk and develop a mitigation plan.

questions.e: C. Have a meeting with the mayor and explain the importance of the new train station to the city: It’s essential to ensure that the mayor understands the strategic importance of the tram station, particularly if there is external pressure to stop the project. A clear discussion can help align the mayor’s support and strengthen the project’s backing. D. Conduct regular meetings with the neighbors to get their buy-in for the project: Direct engagement with the neighbors is crucial. Regular meetings help to address their concerns, clarify misunderstandings, and gather support, reducing the likelihood of legal action or continued resistance.

questions.q: A project needs to purchase a specific piece of equipment, as stated in the project documents and approved by the project sponsor. The procurement division is questioning the need to buy the specific brand of equipment and has suggested buying a cheaper alternative instead. What should the project manager have done earlier in the project to ensure the purchase of the specific equipment? *

o.t: Communicated the project charter to the procurement division.
Included a procurement division member on the project team.
Reminded the project sponsor about the procurement division's reputation.
Communicated the project management plan to the procurement division.

questions.e: Communicating the project management plan to the procurement division ensures that they are fully aware of all project requirements, including the need for specific equipment. This detailed plan includes the rationale behind the choice of equipment and aligns the procurement team with the project's objectives, reducing the likelihood of misunderstandings or suggestions for alternative purchases.

questions.q: A project manager who Is new to an organization is given data that include information related to both project team members and stakeholders. Among other items, this information includes each stakeholder's current role, previous and current projects in which they participated, and their level of organizational influence. In what type of analysis should the project manager use this information? *

o.t: Regression analysis
Stakeholder analysis
Qualitative risk analysis
Decision tree analysis

questions.e: Stakeholder analysis involves identifying and analyzing stakeholders to understand their influence, interests, and impact on the project. The information provided, such as roles, project involvement, and level of influence, is critical for performing a stakeholder analysis to effectively manage and engage stakeholders throughout the project.

questions.q: During the execution phase, the project manager discovered that the deliverables are not meeting the quality specifications requested by the main stakeholder. This has caused the schedule performance index (SPI) to deteriorate from 0.98 to 0.72 and the cost performance index (CPI) from 1.5 to 1.1. What action should the project manager take to mitigate the issue of the deliverables being rejected during the next iteration? *

o.t: Submit a change request to prioritize resolutions for the quality issue to minimize the impact on the rest of the deliverables.
Reinforce the definition of done (DoD) during sprint planning so that the team has a common understanding of expectations.
Assure that the product backlog is properly prioritized to avoid dependencies that cause rejection.
Create a dedicated sprint to complete all of the pending specifications from previous sprints.

questions.e: Reinforcing the definition of done (DoD) during sprint planning ensures that all team members have a clear and shared understanding of what is required for deliverables to meet quality specifications. This helps in preventing quality issues and rework, thereby improving the likelihood that deliverables will be accepted and meet the stakeholder's expectations.

questions.q: During the third iteration, the team encounters a major delay that has not had significant improvements over the last few weeks. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Retrospect frequently and suggest improvements.
Incorporate a predictive approach for this element.
Implement mitigation strategies for this element.
Request additional team members to help with improvements.

questions.e: Frequent retrospectives allow the team to regularly reflect on their processes and performance, identify issues, and suggest improvements. This iterative approach helps the team adapt and find solutions to delays or other problems they encounter, fostering continuous improvement and preventing similar issues in the future.

questions.q: A project manager is responsible for providing a budget estimate for a long-term project that will be executed over several years. Which essential task should the project manager implement at this phase? *

o.t: Include key risks in the cost baseline.
Perform an analogous estimate.
Perform a bottom-up estimate.
Include projected inflation rates.

questions.e: For a long-term project that spans several years, it is crucial to account for projected inflation rates in the budget estimate. This ensures that the cost estimates remain accurate and realistic over the duration of the project, considering the potential increase in prices and costs over time.

questions.q: A project manager receives a request for proposal (RFP) from a client. The client is very clear about the requirements. A requirements analysis must be done in the first month of the project, and the client wants to see a demo of the work completed every two weeks. What project approach should the project manager use? *

o.t: Iterative for the requirements analysis and delivery phases of the project.
Agile for all of the phases of the project, including the requirements analysis and delivery.
Predictive for the requirements analysis and agile for delivery of the project.
Predictive for the requirements analysis and delivery phases of the project.

questions.e: Using a predictive approach for the requirements analysis ensures that the client's clear requirements are thoroughly analyzed and documented upfront. An agile approach for the delivery phase allows for flexibility and regular demos every two weeks, aligning with the client's request for frequent progress updates and feedback.

questions.q: A team has been working on a project for several months, but the completion date is unclear because the scope is changing frequently as new knowledge is gained. Some deliverables have already been completed, but when new stakeholders join the team, they complain that project outcomes are not meeting business goals. How can the project manager prevent this situation from happening in the future? *

o.t: Create a prioritized backlog and define iteration review sessions with stakeholders.
Create a detailed work breakdown structure (WBS) and milestone schedule approved by all stakeholders.
Schedule a daily meeting to review team performance and impediments.
Schedule a kick-off meeting for every project phase to share the project management plan with all stakeholders.

questions.e: Creating a prioritized backlog ensures that the most important and valuable items are worked on first, aligning the project outcomes with business goals. Defining iteration review sessions with stakeholders provides regular opportunities for feedback and adjustments, helping to manage scope changes and ensure that deliverables meet stakeholder expectations and business objectives.

questions.q: A team member has indicated their user story will not be finished until the end of the iteration as their functional manager has requested they assist in resolving a high-priority production issue. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Discuss with the product owner that the user story will not be completed this iteration.
Meet with the team member's functional manager to try to remove the impediment.
Tell the project team member not to work on the production issue and to inform their manager.
Escalate the issue to the project sponsor to resolve and adjust the project burndown chart.

questions.e: Meeting with the team member's functional manager allows the project manager to discuss the conflict and seek a resolution that addresses both the high-priority production issue and the project needs. This approach helps in understanding the urgency and importance of the production issue and potentially finding a way to manage both responsibilities without significant impact on the project's progress.

questions.q: At the daily project meeting, team members are complaining about receiving emails from their functional managers to support other non project-related tasks. This is having a negative impact on the team's productivity. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Ask the product owner to speak with the functional managers to ensure future requirements come through the product owner.
Log this as a risk in the risk register and continue to monitor the issue at subsequent meetings.
Address this concern with the functional managers to ensure there will be no further delays.
Schedule a meeting with all of the functional managers to resolve the resource conflicts.

questions.e: Scheduling a meeting with all the functional managers allows the project manager to directly address the resource conflict issue. This meeting provides an opportunity to discuss and negotiate how to prioritize project tasks versus other non-project-related tasks, ensuring that team members can focus on their project responsibilities without undue interruptions. This approach helps to align expectations and fosters collaboration between the project and functional managers, ultimately improving team productivity.

questions.q: A project manager is assigned to a new project to deliver a product at the end of the year. The project manager was informed by the vendor that a core component could not be shipped on time, which will impact the schedule. What should project manager to do next to minimize the impact on the project? *

o.t: Schedule a meeting with all stakeholders to extend the project deadline.
Replace the vendor with a new vendor who can offer the component on time.
Add an item to the next status review to make stakeholders aware of the vendor issue.
Review and update the issue log and determine if any alternative components can be offered.

questions.e: Updating the issue log ensures that the vendor issue is formally documented and tracked. Determining if any alternative components can be offered helps in identifying potential solutions to mitigate the impact on the project schedule. This approach focuses on problem-solving and finding ways to keep the project on track without immediately resorting to more drastic measures such as changing vendors or extending deadlines.

questions.q: A project manager is hired by a global company. The project manager is an agile specialist and is tasked with supporting the project team to reduce rework and dissatisfaction. How should the project manager address these objectives? *

o.t: Decrease the scope of the portfolio and send new solutions to the customer.
Deliver a schedule with the portfolio timeline and delivery to the customer.
Adopt an incremental cycle of delivering value to the customer.
Prepare deliveries with more details to satisfy the customer.

questions.e: Adopting an incremental cycle of delivering value to the customer aligns with agile principles. It involves delivering small, usable segments of the product frequently, allowing for regular feedback and adjustments. This approach helps reduce rework by ensuring that customer feedback is incorporated early and often, leading to higher satisfaction and a product that better meets customer needs.

questions.q: During the retrospective ceremony, the agile team is talking about the product owner’s expectations not being met. What should the project manager have done at the beginning of the project? *

o.t: Defined the expected agile team contribution in the creation of the backlog.
Assessed the capabilities of the agile team and planned for the required training.
Defined the team ground rules and shared project vision.
Communicated project vision and sprint goals clearly to the team.

questions.e: Clear communication of the project vision and sprint goals at the beginning of the project ensures that the agile team understands what is expected and aligns their efforts accordingly. This helps in meeting the product owner's expectations and achieving the desired outcomes. Effective communication helps in setting a common understanding and direction for the team.

questions.q: During the execution of a project, the finance team identified that they were not involved in building the business case for the project and will not approve the estimated return on investment (ROI). What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Revisit the communications management plan and make necessary adjustments.
Revisit the scope management plan and note this as a risk.
Schedule a meeting with the product owner and finance team to agree on course corrections.
Continue developing based on the project management plan and address the issue post delivery.

questions.e: Scheduling a meeting with the product owner and finance team allows the project manager to address the issue directly with the key stakeholders. This meeting can help in understanding the finance team's concerns, revisiting the business case, and agreeing on necessary course corrections to ensure the project's ROI is acceptable and aligns with financial expectations. This proactive approach helps in resolving the issue early and maintaining project alignment with organizational goals.

questions.q: Due to delays on some activities one of the project team members has increased the scope without any approval. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Remove the changes to match the original requirements.
Add team members to the project to avoid more schedule delays.
Evaluate the impacts of the changes that were made to the project.
Update project documentation with the new scope.

questions.e: The project manager should first evaluate the impacts of the unauthorized changes on the project's scope, schedule, cost, and quality. Understanding these impacts allows for an informed decision on whether to keep the changes, revert them, or make other adjustments. After this evaluation, the project manager can follow the change control process to seek the necessary approvals or take corrective actions.

questions.q: A project sponsor asks the project team to add an enhancement to the project. How should the project manager address this request? *

o.t: Check if the budget can cover the enhancement.
Accept the request because it came from the project sponsor.
Refuse the project sponsor's request because it is out of scope.
Validate the proposed change's impact on the project.

questions.e: Validating the proposed change's impact on the project involves assessing how the enhancement will affect the project's scope, schedule, cost, quality, and other critical factors. This allows the project manager to provide a clear understanding of the consequences of implementing the change. Based on this analysis, the project manager can then follow the change control process to make an informed decision.

questions.q: A project manager for a strategic initiative realizes a new stakeholder is interested in the project and wants to ensure the stakeholder is fully aware of the goals, objectives, benefits, and risks of the project. What should the project manager do to enhance the success of the project? *

o.t: Add the new stakeholder to the communications management plan.
Share the project status reports with the new stakeholder.
Update the stakeholder engagement plan.
Schedule a meeting with the new stakeholder.

questions.e: The stakeholder engagement plan outlines how the project manager will communicate with, involve, and manage stakeholders throughout the project. When a new stakeholder expresses interest, it’s crucial to update this plan to ensure the stakeholder is appropriately engaged, informed, and their expectations are managed. This update includes determining the best ways to communicate the project's goals, objectives, benefits, and risks to them and how frequently they should be updated. By updating the stakeholder engagement plan, the project manager ensures that the new stakeholder is integrated into the communication strategy, and the engagement approach is aligned with the project's needs and the stakeholder’s level of influence or interest.

questions.q: The portfolio management office wants to cut costs by suspending some ongoing projects that do not directly support the organizational strategy. The project manager has invested too many resources into one of the projects to be suspended, but the portfolio management office has not backed down on their plan. What should the project manager do to continue the project? *

o.t: Meet with the project team and revise the project goals.
Update the project charter to make it align with organizational strategy.
Demonstrate the project alignment to the organizational strategy.
Escalate the issue with the project sponsor to request support.

questions.e: To continue the project, the project manager needs to show how the project supports the organizational strategy. By demonstrating the alignment between the project's goals and the broader organizational strategy, the project manager can justify the project's continuation and highlight its strategic importance. This approach is more effective than revising the project goals or escalating the issue without supporting evidence.

questions.q: During a retrospective review, many project team members say they are not completing tasks during the iterations because of interruptions and requests for help from other teams. As a team facilitator, what should the project manager do to avoid this? *

o.t: Identify the problem's root causes and define the ground rules with all project team members to minimize interferences.
Hire a coach to help all project teams to improve their abilities to solve problems on their own.
Reunite with the project team members affected and tell them not to reduce the team's capacity.
Recommend to the project team members that they should improve their planning and make their stones smaller.

questions.e: Identifying the root causes of the interruptions and defining ground rules helps address the underlying issues that are causing the interruptions. Establishing clear ground rules can help set expectations for team interactions and minimize interferences, allowing team members to focus on their tasks and improve productivity.

questions.q: A project is delayed due to an undelivered component, which was caused by a conflict between the procurement lead and the contracts manager. The project manager schedules a meeting with the two stakeholders to resolve the issue. What role does the project manager play in this situation? *

o.t: Accommodator.
Mediator.
Arbitrator.
Conciliator.

questions.e: In this situation, the project manager acts as a mediator. A mediator facilitates communication between the conflicting parties (the procurement lead and the contracts manager) to help them reach a mutually acceptable resolution. The project manager's role is to guide the discussion, ensure that each party's concerns are heard, and assist them in finding a solution that resolves the conflict and allows the project to move forward.

questions.q: In analyzing a project for monthly status reporting, the project manager notices that the schedule performance index (SPI) is 0.75 and the cost performance index (CPI) is 1. 25. The project manager must provide the first project status review soon and wants to emphasize that the project is under control. How should the project manager report the project status to key stakeholders? *

o.t: Prepare a detailed presentation for stakeholders on earned value including how it is calculated and the project's current earned value results.
Report that the project is behind schedule but that an additional experienced resource can be added to stay within schedule and maintain the budget.
Perform a detailed root cause analysis utilizing a pareto chart and fishbone diagrams to demonstrate that the project is under control.
Report that the project is not tracking as expected, but is still under control since the next project milestone is over a month away.

questions.e: The SPI of 0.75 indicates that the project is behind schedule, while the CPI of 1.25 indicates that the project is under budget. Emphasizing that the project is under control despite being behind schedule, and presenting a plan to add an experienced resource to catch up on the schedule while maintaining the budget, provides a proactive solution to address the delay. This approach shows stakeholders that the project manager is aware of the issues and has a plan to bring the project back on track.

questions.q: An agile project team is working on an infrastructure product to be delivered incrementally over several iterations. Midway through the third iteration, the whole company is informed that the operating systems supported by the infrastructure will be terminated in the upcoming quarter. Several thousand machines will be impacted by this change. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Prioritize the upgrade of project machines with the IT department.
Inform the product owner and request more project resources.
Schedule a session with stakeholders to understand the impact.
Add product backlog items to prioritize operating system stories.

questions.e: When faced with a significant change that impacts the project scope or environment, such as the termination of operating systems, the first action should be to engage with stakeholders to assess the impact. This is in line with the agile principle of collaboration and early stakeholder engagement. By scheduling a session with stakeholders, the project manager can gather insights on the implications of the change, which is essential for informed decision-making and planning. This approach is supported by the PMBOKGuide, which emphasizes the importance of stakeholder engagement and communication when dealing with project changes. Additionally, the Professional in Business Analysis (PBA) materials highlight the need for business analysis to understand the requirements and constraints of the stakeholders, which is critical in this scenario to determine the next steps for the project.

questions.q: A project manager is in the middle of a project when one of the key project team members needs to take an unexpected and prolonged leave of absence. The project is ahead of schedule and running under budget. Which two actions should the project manager take initially to resolve this problem? (Choose two) *

o.t: Check the risk register for a prepared response to a resource being suddenly unavailable.
Check if the team member's activities are sufficiently documented to facilitate handover.
Check the project's responsibility assignment matrix (RAM) to determine which activities will be affected.
Reassign responsibilities across the remaining members using the available float for training.
Obtain the project sponsors support to replace the team member on leave.

questions.e: A. Checking the risk register helps in identifying any pre-planned responses to resource unavailability, ensuring that the project manager can quickly implement an effective strategy. C. Reviewing the project's responsibility assignment matrix (RAM) helps identify which activities are affected by the team member's absence, enabling the project manager to address the immediate impacts on the project.

questions.q: A project manager for a large multiyear industrial project has a project with diversified stakeholders from various geographical areas. Recently, the project manager encountered an issue with stakeholder engagement. Which two tools should the project manager use to determine the underlying reason for why engagement is not having the planned effect? (Choose two) *

o.t: Five whys.
Communications management plan.
Ishikawa diagrams.
Issue log.
Open-space meetings.

questions.e: A. Five whys. Explanation: The "Five Whys" technique helps identify the root cause of a problem by repeatedly asking "why" until the fundamental issue is uncovered. This method is effective for understanding underlying reasons for engagement issues. C. Ishikawa diagrams. Explanation: Ishikawa diagrams, also known as fishbone diagrams, help visualize the causes of a specific problem. This tool can be used to systematically identify various factors contributing to the engagement issue.

questions.q: An intern is replacing a critical resource midway through a sprint. To help the intern get up to speed, the project manager assigns a senior engineer in the team as the intern's mentor . Two months later, the project goes into critical status, delaying the release milestone by a month. What should the project manager have done to avoid this scenario? *

o.t: Convinced the critical resource to remain on the project.
Requested an experienced resource as a replacement.
Allocated additional time for mentoring.
Negotiated additional time to complete the project.

questions.e: The delay in the project suggests that the intern was not able to ramp up quickly enough to match the productivity of the critical resource they replaced. While mentoring was provided, it was not sufficient to prevent project delays. The best course of action for the project manager would have been to request an experienced replacement rather than relying on an intern. This would have minimized the impact on the project's schedule and reduced the risk of delays.

questions.q: After gathering all the requirements for a project with dependencies on external stakeholders, the project team is finishing the second iteration. At this point, the project manager learns about a possible change in regulations that would prevent the product launch. What should the project manager do to realize benefits? *

o.t: Add an entry in the risk log.
Implement the changes.
Review target benefits.
Improve the team's velocity.

questions.e: By adding the potential regulatory change to the risk log, the project manager can formally recognize the risk and plan appropriate responses. This allows the team to monitor the situation and develop mitigation strategies to address the potential impact on the project.

questions.q: A new project manager learns the work assigned to the team has already been decomposed to its lowest level. The project manager reviews the work and feels some additional useful information is missing. What should the project manager review? *

o.t: The project charter and scope statement.
The requirements traceability matrix.
The business requirement documents (BRD).
The WBS dictionary.

questions.e: The WBS dictionary provides detailed information about each element in the Work Breakdown Structure (WBS), including descriptions of work, deliverables, and other pertinent details. This can help the project manager identify any missing information necessary for project execution.

questions.q: A project manager has been assigned to take over an existing software project. The project manager inherited a lean team comprised of key stakeholders, subject matter experts (SMEs), and senior developers. While reviewing the project status with the team, the project manager observes that the team seems to lack direction and enthusiasm. What should the new project manager do? *

o.t: Ensure everyone performs their assigned tasks as planned.
Organize frequent team building sessions and update the risk register.
Meet with the project sponsor and propose a corrective action for the project.
Encourage participation in decision making and empower the team.

questions.e: Encouraging team participation in decision-making and empowering team members can increase their sense of ownership and motivation. This approach can help in providing direction and boosting enthusiasm among team members.

questions.q: A company has agreed to run a transformation project using agile approaches. During the implementation, there is pushback from the functional groups that the project is moving too fast. What should the project manager have done at the beginning of the project to prevent this from happening? *

o.t: Circulated the project charter.
Assessed the organizational culture.
Determined the level of maturity of the employees.
Communicated the project schedule.

questions.e: Assessing the organizational culture helps the project manager understand how receptive the functional groups are to agile approaches. This allows for the development of strategies to manage change effectively and align the pace of the project with the organization’s capacity for adopting new methodologies.

questions.q: A project manager is tracking a project, but a key stakeholder will not accept the project's key performance indicator (KPI) results. Which tool or technique should the project manager use? *

o.t: Autocratic decision making.
Expert judgment.
Context diagram.
Change control tools.

questions.e: Using expert judgment involves consulting with subject matter experts to validate the KPI results and address the stakeholder's concerns. This can help in providing a credible basis for the results and gaining stakeholder acceptance.

questions.q: A technical manager newly appointed by the client, visits the project site to verify the project deliverables. The technical manager feels that the project manager has not been providing enough information. What should the project manager do first to resolve this situation? *

o.t: Update the issue log and escalate to the project sponsor.
Identify the lack of information as a risk and update the risk register.
Schedule more frequent meetings with the technical manager.
Review and update the stakeholder engagement plan.

questions.e: The first step should be to review and update the stakeholder engagement plan to ensure that the information needs of the new technical manager are being met. By understanding the specific information requirements of the technical manager and updating the plan accordingly, the project manager can ensure that appropriate communication channels and frequencies are established to provide the necessary information.

questions.q: The Scrum team working with the quality department has been shifting away from the Business unit due to unclear product requirements. It is now the third sprint and both teams have been at a standstill for a few days. What should the project leader do to solve this situation? *

o.t: Analyze the problem with both teams to figure out If pan of the work must be redone.
Select new team members in an effort to obtain fresh ideas to solve the impasse.
Demand that the business team stop wasting time and define final requirements for the product.
Tell the business team and Scrum team to continue following the initial plan.

questions.e: Analyzing the problem with both teams allows for a collaborative approach to identify the root cause of the issue and determine if any work needs to be redone. This promotes clear communication and helps both teams understand and address the unclear product requirements.

questions.q: During a network upgrade for a company, the client informs the project manager that a government representative notified the client about a separate project that will affect the network upgrade. Any change in the upgrade will impact the project's cost and schedule. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Perform an impact analysis with subject matter experts (SMEs).
Inform the government representative about the impact of the separate project.
Implement a change request to increase the budget and schedule.
Consult and update the risk register with the project stakeholders.

questions.e: Conducting an impact analysis with SMEs helps to understand the potential effects on the project's cost, schedule, and scope. This information is critical before taking any further steps, such as informing stakeholders or implementing change requests.

questions.q: A company is moving its headquarters to another city. The project manager responsible for the assignment has been using a predictive approach during the transition. However, the information systems will be migrated using an agile approach. The project manager needs to decide which kind of control to sign with the vendor responsible for migrating the systems. How should the project manager address this situation? *

o.t: Negotiate payment after all project migration is completed.
Sign a single agreement for the whole project.
Use fixed-price increments as user stories are completed.
Confirm payment after each project retrospective.

questions.e: This method ensures that the vendor is paid for each deliverable incrementally, promoting accountability and allowing for adjustments based on the progress and quality of work. It provides a balance between predictability in costs and flexibility in project execution.

questions.q: A project manager is leading a project with several stakeholders in other functional areas of the company One of these stakeholders has just been promoted to lead another functional area, and remains a stakeholder for this project. What should the project manager have the project team update to ensure proper communications to stakeholders? *

o.t: Project management plan.
Stakeholder engagement plan.
Stakeholder register.
Communications management plan.

questions.e: When a stakeholder's role changes, it is important to ensure that their communication needs and the way they are kept informed about the project are updated. The Communications Management Plan outlines how project information will be communicated to stakeholders, including the frequency, method, and type of information to be shared. Updating this plan ensures that the newly promoted stakeholder continues to receive the appropriate communications relevant to their new role.

questions.q: A project manager is in rapid development mode on a joint application development module. The company wants delivery to occur in two weeks. The module needs to be integrated with other modules on a similar timeline, but release management has a three-week backlog. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Push the team to deliver more so that the modules are developed and rolled out according to management's request.
Speak to the stakeholders to resolve the bottleneck and see how the entire process can be streamlined.
Have the team work toward the tighter deadline so that integration will be easier.
Speak to the team and slow the current pace to ensure the team is in alignment with the release date.

questions.e: Engaging with stakeholders to address the backlog in release management helps to identify potential solutions and streamline the process. This approach ensures that the integration and delivery schedules are aligned without overburdening the team or compromising the quality of work.

questions.q: A Scrum team working in an aircraft manufacturing company has completed Its first iteration for a critical project. It is very Important for the project sponsor to complete the project on time and under budget A burndown chart indicates that the project is behind schedule. Which two actions should the project manager take to manage Impediments and improve the team's velocity? (Choose two) *

o.t: Look for processes that cause bottlenecks and slow down the team's agility.
Assign the items with high complexity lo senior developers.
Empower the learn to make decisions to remove impediments.
Work with the team to remove impediments as quickly as possible.
Move the items with high complexity to the last iterations.

questions.e: A. Look for processes that cause bottlenecks and slow down the team's agility: Identifying and addressing bottlenecks can help streamline processes and improve the team's overall efficiency and velocity. By removing or mitigating these bottlenecks, the team can work more effectively. D. Work with the team to remove impediments as quickly as possible: Actively working with the team to identify and remove impediments ensures that obstacles are addressed promptly, allowing the team to maintain momentum and improve their velocity.

questions.q: A project management team received news that a competitor has released the latest version of a program. What should the team do next? *

o.t: Review the project plan to evaluate if any updates should be made.
Crash the existing schedule with additional resources to deliver more features.
Stop the project immediately as the market opportunity has already been missed.
Continue with the project plan and target delivery date as expected.

questions.e: Reviewing the project plan allows the team to assess the impact of the competitor's release on their project. They can then decide if any adjustments or updates are necessary to remain competitive and meet market needs.

questions.q: During the initiation stage of a multimedia exhibition-design project the project manager is developing the project management plan. What should the project manager do to complete this task? *

o.t: Benchmark other similar exhibitions' deliverable lists and final outcomes.
Initiate a survey to solicit end-customer opinions and prioritize exhibition contents.
Clarify the high-level business requirements with the event organizer as a basis for forming the deliverables list.
Initiate an additional services agreement in case the key deliverables list was not clearly stated in the contract.

questions.e: Clarifying the high-level business requirements with the event organizer ensures that the project deliverables align with the organizer's expectations and objectives. This provides a solid foundation for developing a comprehensive project management plan.

questions.q: The project team finds that the latest delivery from a vendor is missing a critical component, which will likely delay the project inspite of corrective measures. What should the project manager do to communicate this message? *

o.t: Ask the vendor to identify the stakeholders affected, create an action plan and determine an implementation date.
Draft a warning letter to the vendor ask internal stakeholders to comment and solicit stakeholder support to hold the vendor accountable.
Identify the worst-case scenario, put it into the project risk register, share the register with all project stakeholders, and raise an alert.
Contact department managers who are identified as stakeholders, solicit concern, and provide updates to the situation.

questions.e: Effective communication in project management involves ensuring that the right stakeholders are informed about critical issues that may impact the project. In this scenario, since the missing component could cause a delay despite corrective actions, the project manager must proactively engage the relevant department managers (stakeholders) to gather concerns and keep them updated. This approach helps in risk mitigation, coordination, and stakeholder alignment on potential impacts and solutions.

questions.q: A team is working on a project using a hybrid approach, and they are facing a lot of obstacles and blockers from some stakeholders. What should the project manager do to improve project performance? *

o.t: Ask stakeholders to communicate with the project manager and not directly with the team.
Empower the team members to remove obstacles and blockers.
Address and remove obstacles and blockers for the team.
Add blockers to the issue log and risk management plan.

questions.e: The project manager should take a proactive approach in removing obstacles and blockers to improve project performance. This allows the team to focus on their tasks without hindrances, leading to a more efficient and productive workflow. By addressing these issues, the project manager ensures that the team can maintain momentum and meet project objectives effectively.

questions.q: A company is transitioning from a predictive to agile delivery of projects. Based on the requirements, the project team estimates the budget and decides to use a fixed-price contract with its vendor. However, during the execution of the project, the requirements evolve and priorities start to change constantly, which puts the project and the estimate at completion (EAC) off by 40%. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Send a detailed status report highlighting the issue with funding to all of the stakeholders.
Submit a change request to the financial manager to increase the funding and continue as is.
Meet with the stakeholders to recommend the use of a time and materials (T&M) contract to address the problem.
Wait until the next gate review meeting to highlight the risk of low funds to the stakeholders.

questions.e: In an agile environment, requirements often evolve, and priorities can change frequently. A fixed-price contract may not provide the flexibility needed to accommodate these changes, leading to significant budget overruns. By recommending a time and materials (T&M) contract, the project manager can address the issue by allowing for more flexibility in accommodating changing requirements and ensuring that the project can proceed without the constraints of a fixed budget.

questions.q: A key project stakeholder who was a big supporter and motivator for the project team is leaving the organization. The project team is experiencing low morale and poor teamwork. What should the project manager do to improve morale? *

o.t: Identify the wants and aspirations of the team.
Build team connections and emotional bonds.
Forge consensus through team participation.
Set goals and push the team to achieve the goals.

questions.e: Build team connections and emotional bonds focuses on addressing the root cause of low morale by fostering strong interpersonal relationships and emotional bonds within the team. This approach helps create a supportive and cohesive team environment, which can improve morale and teamwork. Building connections can help fill the motivational gap left by the departing stakeholder and enhance the overall team dynamics.

questions.q: A project is ending and the final deliverables have been accepted by the customer. The project team is pleased that the project was a success: however, some groups within the customer's organization believe the objective of the project was not met. What should the project manager have done to avoid this issue? *

o.t: Distributed a detailed quality management plan to the key stakeholders.
Included the final report during the closing phase to ensure common understanding.
Identified key stakeholders and included all of them in project agreement discussions.
Performed project reporting according to the communications management plan.

questions.e: To avoid misunderstandings and ensure that the objectives of the project are met from the perspective of all stakeholders, the project manager should identify all key stakeholders early in the project and involve them in project agreement discussions. This helps ensure that the expectations and requirements of all relevant parties are understood and agreed upon, reducing the risk of dissatisfaction at the project's conclusion.

questions.q: A software system is being built for a company. Once the system is in production, the team would like to collect usage data to evaluate the delivered value. Which evaluation practice should the project lead use to obtain accurate usage data?

o.t: Send out a questionnaire to all users regarding the most useful features.
Embed a feedback form into the system for users to respond.
Interview a sampling of users to obtain the usage data.
Build the functionality in the software to collect the operational usage data.

questions.e: Interviews can help the project lead understand user experiences, identify pain points, and gather detailed feedback on the system's features and performance. This evaluation practice goes beyond mere data collection and helps in gaining a deeper understanding of the delivered value from the user's perspective.

questions.q: At the end of the last iteration, the customer rejects the deliverables since they did not meet the customer's expectations. What should the project manager have been done to prevent this situation? *

o.t: Involved the customer more in the planning process for the project, and ensured agreement on the proceedings.
Included all relevant criteria in the agreed upon definition of done (DoD), and crafted a shared product vision.
Provided the customer with the backlog and the specified user stories at the beginning of the iteration.
Developed the DoD in close cooperation with all stakeholders to ensure their expectations were included.

questions.e: Developing the definition of done (DoD) in close cooperation with all stakeholders ensures that their expectations are clearly understood and included in the criteria for completed deliverables. This collaborative approach helps align the project team and stakeholders on what constitutes an acceptable deliverable, reducing the likelihood of misunderstandings and rejections at the end of iterations.

questions.q: A project has recently Kicked off. The project manager observes that there are different expectations among the project team members. These growing misunderstandings are affecting team productivity. Which document should the project manager use as a guide to resolve the issue? *

o.t: Project charter.
Stakeholder register.
Team charter.
Project organization charts.

questions.e: The team charter is a document that outlines the team's purpose, values, agreements, and operational guidelines. It helps set clear expectations for team behavior and collaboration. By referring to the team charter, the project manager can address misunderstandings and align the team on their shared goals and expectations, thereby improving productivity and cohesion.

questions.q: In a global project, the project manager has to plan and manage communication between the team members and stakeholders in order to ensure the project will remain on track and achieve its goals. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Consider cultural differences among stakeholders.
Conduct an integration meeting among all stakeholders.
Schedule communication training for management-level stakeholders.
Understand how political aspects can affect the project.

questions.e: In a global project, cultural differences can significantly impact how communication is perceived and understood among team members and stakeholders. By considering and addressing these cultural differences, the project manager can ensure more effective and inclusive communication. This approach helps in building better relationships, preventing misunderstandings, and keeping the project on track to achieve its goals.

questions.q: A company is implementing a new system. The project manager has identified that it is best to complete this project using a mix of Scrum and Kanban methodologies. The product owner is confused as to how to start delivering the functionalities required. How should the project manager assist the product owner? *

o.t: Coach the product owner on how to create a product backlog.
Encourage the team to subdivide the project tasks.
Create a work breakdown structure (WBS) and explain the deliverables to the product owner.
Discuss the product owner's responsibilities within the project team.

questions.e: In a project using Scrum and Kanban methodologies, the product backlog is a critical tool for managing and prioritizing work. By coaching the product owner on how to create and manage a product backlog, the project manager ensures that the product owner understands how to prioritize and organize the required functionalities. This helps the team start delivering value incrementally and effectively.

questions.q: During the design phase of a project the project manager notices that the schedule performance index (SPI) is 1 . 8 and the cost performance index (CPI) is 0 . 1. In a weekly meeting with top management, the project manager reports concerns about these indicators. However the most concerned person was the project sponsor who said that if the trend continues, they will be forced to prematurely close the project. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Monitor the project sponsor but understand that it is normal to spend more money in the design phase of a project.
Stop crashing the schedule.
Manage the project sponsor closely and revise the project's resource management plan to improve indicators.
Use a resource-levelling technique.

questions.e: With a CPI of 0.1, the project is significantly over budget. Crashing the schedule often increases costs because it involves adding resources to speed up project completion. Stopping the crashing will help control these costs and improve the CPI. This action provides an immediate response to the cost issue, which is crucial given the sponsor's concern about potentially closing the project.

questions.q: A company has decided to implement a new archiving system. A data breach occurred during the implementation of the project. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Implement the planned risk response to handle the issue.
Review possible alternative documentation methods with team.
Update the risk register with the risk and proposed impact.
Ask the team to fix the system to resolve the issue.

questions.e: Implementing the planned risk response ensures immediate and effective action based on pre-defined strategies, minimizing the impact of the data breach promptly.

questions.q: During the implementation stage of a project. a newly appointed team leader approaches the project manager to verify the team's tasks and schedule. The work did not go as planned due to the team leader's lack of management experience. This could cause delays for the project. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Ask the human resources director to appoint a senior team leader.
Inform the project sponsor about the possible delay.
Directly manage the project team to avoid project delays.
Provide mentoring to the newly appointed team leader.

questions.e: Providing mentoring to the newly appointed team leader is the best course of action. This approach addresses the root cause of the issue by helping the team leader gain the necessary management skills and knowledge. It fosters their development and improves their ability to manage the team effectively, which in turn helps to avoid project delays and enhances overall project performance.

questions.q: A company is initiating a project to enhance one of its existing products. All of its products are developed internally. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Ensure the stakeholder engagement plan is accurate and properly documented.
Review the lessons learned from the previous project.
Identify the risk of implementing the new solution and evaluate the impact on the project.
Create a lessons learned document for the initiation phase.

questions.e: Reviewing the lessons learned from previous projects can provide valuable insights and help avoid repeating past mistakes. This information is crucial for initiating a new project, as it can guide planning and execution, improve decision-making, and enhance the chances of project success. By leveraging past experiences, the project manager can better anticipate challenges and implement effective strategies from the outset.

questions.q: During project execution, the project manager discovered that a key deliverable was missing from the scope of work. After investigation, the project manager and the team discovered that the missing deliverable will impact the critical path. What should the project manager do to avoid future delays? *

o.t: Submit a change request.
Add additional resources to the project.
Update the scope of work.
Review the risk management plan.

questions.e: When a key deliverable is missing from the scope of work and impacts the critical path, the project manager should submit a change request. This ensures that the necessary adjustments to the project scope, schedule, and resources are formally reviewed and approved. The change request process allows for a structured approach to incorporating the missing deliverable into the project, minimizing the impact on the critical path and avoiding future delays.

questions.q: In a software development project, the product owner and development team agree on a sprint backlog. The highest priority in the backlog is to build a payment module. The team worked on the module during the first half of the sprint, but now two developers want to spend the rest of the sprint focusing on refactoring another feature that might create issues in the future. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Let the developers focus on the refactoring work and discuss it in the retrospective.
Restate to the developers the importance of focusing and meeting the sprint goal.
Praise the developers for their proactivity and focus on quality.
Escalate the issue to the developers’ functional managers.

questions.e: The primary objective of the sprint is to complete the agreed-upon sprint backlog, which includes the highest-priority item, the payment module. Ensuring the team stays focused on the sprint goal helps maintain alignment with the project's priorities and deliverables. Refactoring can be important but should not detract from achieving the sprint goal.

questions.q: A Scrum team has committed to delivering a specific capability in their first release. Multiple operational issues have prevented the developer from delivering key capabilities. The technical lead has also given notice that they are resigning from the company. What should the project manager have the Scrum team do to recover from these issues? *

o.t: Review constraints in the ongoing sprint planning and evaluate options for the release plan.
Stop the sprint and replan and prioritize the backlog to reduce resource levels.
Consult the resource management plan for an appropriate response.
Continue with existing sprint plans to ensure some of the scope will be delivered.

questions.e: When a Scrum team faces multiple operational issues and the resignation of a key team member, it's crucial to reassess the situation and adjust plans accordingly. Reviewing constraints in the ongoing sprint planning and evaluating options for the release plan allows the team to address current challenges, re-prioritize tasks, and make informed decisions on how to proceed. This approach helps to ensure that the team can adapt to the changes and still aim to deliver value in the release.

questions.q: A company has an existing contract to maintain and enhance a client's customer database. The company's legal department informs the project manager that a new piece of legislature requiring stricter protection of customer information might soon be signed into law. The law will require additional security features to be implemented into the database the project manager is maintaining. These features are not included in the scope of the current contract. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Ask the legal department to raise the issue in the next contract negotiation with the customer.
Seek the project sponsor's support to influence the client to amend the contract immediately.
Update the risk register to include this issue and discuss the appropriate risk response plans with the project sponsor and client.
Wait until the legal requirements are finalized so the change in scope can be concretely defined.

questions.e: When a potential legislative change may impact the project, it's essential to proactively manage the risk. Updating the risk register to include this issue ensures that it is formally recognized and tracked. Discussing appropriate risk response plans with the project sponsor and client allows for collaborative planning and preparation for potential changes. This proactive approach helps to mitigate risks and ensure that all parties are aware and ready to adapt as needed.

questions.q: A large corporation is transforming itself from a predictive to agile approach. A project team with knowledge of agile practices is experiencing significant conflicts with the executives regarding the processes to be followed. How should these conflicts be resolved? *

o.t: Include the executives in team retrospectives.
Train the executives on agile practices.
Negotiate with the executives and agree on a process.
Request that the executives use agile practices.

questions.e: Training the executives on agile practices helps bridge the knowledge gap between the project team and the executives. This approach ensures that executives understand the benefits and principles of agile methodologies, which can lead to better support and alignment with the project team's processes. It addresses the root cause of the conflict by providing the necessary knowledge and context, fostering a more collaborative environment.

questions.q: At the end of a meeting a functional manager takes the project manager aside to raise some concerns on behalf of a project team member who is unclear about their role and responsibilities for the project. What should the project manager do in this situation? *

o.t: Develop a work plan for the project team member with the help of the resource manager.
Advise the functional manager and the project team member to review the resource management plan.
Tell the functional manager and the project team member to review the project charter.
Ask the functional manager to create a specific responsible, accountable, consult, and inform (RACI) chart for the team member.

questions.e: The resource management plan outlines the roles and responsibilities of project team members. Advising the functional manager and the team member to review this plan helps clarify their roles and ensures they understand their responsibilities within the project. This approach leverages existing documentation to address the concern efficiently and aligns with standard project management practices.

questions.q: A project started 12 months ago and is currently on iteration 12 of 14. The team has performed well and completed all deliverables on time. However, some team members are starting to complain about the length of the project, creating a risk for lack of performance at this critical stage. What should the project manager do as a servant leader to mitigate this risk? *

o.t: Meet with the team to reinforce their responsibilities and the consequences if the project deliverables are not completed on time.
Apply additional controls to the project deliverables to ensure that all milestones are achieved on time.
Contact the functional manager to ensure that team motivation remains high until the end of the project.
Schedule a team event with the project sponsor to highlight the importance of the project and recognize the work of the team.

questions.e: As a servant leader, the project manager should focus on motivating and recognizing the team to maintain high morale. Scheduling an event with the project sponsor to acknowledge their hard work and emphasize the project's importance can re-energize the team and mitigate the risk of decreased performance.

questions.q: In a newly formed project team one experienced team member is overwhelmed by the complexity of the tasks and is not happy with the project team. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Ask the team member to enter this potential schedule delay in the risk register.
Explain that the tasks are unavoidable and ask the team member to find a solution to overcome the challenges.
Actively listen to the team member and identify ways to support their needs in completing the tasks.
Set up team-building activities with the project team members to reduce tension.

questions.e: Actively listening to the team member and providing support demonstrates empathy and leadership. This approach helps address the team member's concerns, provides the necessary support to overcome challenges, and promotes a positive and collaborative team environment.

questions.q: Project A is critical for the company and must be completed within nine months. The project charter has been signed but the project scope statement has not been prepared Management asks the project manager to move forward with the project without an approved project scope statement. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Escalate the issue to the project sponsor and add it to the risk register.
Refuse to work on the project because management is not following standard project management practices.
Meet with management to explain the potential problems with running a project without a project scope statement.
Start the project with inputs from the project charter to save time.

questions.e: It is essential to communicate the importance of having a clear project scope statement to management. Explaining the potential problems, such as scope creep, misunderstandings, and lack of clear direction, helps management understand the risks involved and the necessity of this document for project success. This approach promotes adherence to standard project management practices and mitigates risks from the outset.

questions.q: During an inspection, the production phase was stopped because the inspector claimed that regulatory labels were missing. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Conduct an expert judgment evaluation.
Review the quality management plan.
Update the lessons learned register.
Review the risk management plan.

questions.e: The quality management plan includes the quality standards and regulatory requirements that the project must meet. Reviewing this plan will help the project manager understand why the regulatory labels were missed and determine the necessary actions to ensure compliance and prevent future issues.

questions.q: A project in the execution phase is behind schedule and is missing some materials. The contractor submits an offer to supply the missing materials and reimburse the cost since the internal procurement process will cause more delay. The project manager does not agree with the costs submitted by the contractor for the missing materials. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Ask the project sponsor to allocate more budget to cover the costs.
Update the procurement management plan and negotiate with the contractor.
Ask the contractor to review the offer and reduce the costs.
Update the procurement strategy and negotiate with the contractor.

questions.e: Updating the procurement management plan allows the project manager to formally document the changes and establish a clear strategy for addressing the missing materials. This step provides a basis for negotiating with the contractor, ensuring that the costs and procurement approach align with the project's objectives and budget constraints.

questions.q: A project selection committee is shortlisting projects for the coming year. Which selection criteria should the project manager recommend? *

o.t: Projects with the least duration.
Projects that maximize the business value.
Projects with maximum revenue generation.
Projects with the least associated risks.

questions.e: Maximizing business value is the most comprehensive criterion, as it considers various factors including revenue generation, strategic alignment, and long-term benefits to the organization. It ensures that the selected projects contribute significantly to the overall goals and priorities of the company.

questions.q: The steering committee has asked a project manager experienced in agile to provide an indication of the time remaining on a medium-sized project. What tools can be used to provide this information? *

o.t: A release burndown chart.
Analysis of the business requirements document.
Story points for the remaining user stories.
Surrogate measurements.

questions.e: A release burndown chart is a visual tool used in Agile projects to track the progress of work against the total scope of a release. It shows the amount of work remaining over time and provides a clear indication of the project's progress and the time remaining to complete it. This is a standard tool in Agile project management for providing status updates and forecasting completion.

questions.q: A project manager is approaching the end of a project, and several tasks are now practically complete and ready for handover to the client. How should the project manager proceed? *

o.t: Update the quality management plan for the overall project.
Ask the client to verify and accept the tasks that have been completed.
Close out the project tasks that have been completed.
Update the communications management plan for the overall project.

questions.e: Client verification and acceptance are essential steps before officially closing out tasks. This ensures that the deliverables meet the client's requirements and expectations, and it formally documents the client's approval, which is crucial for project closure and handover.

questions.q: In a fixed time and budget project the customer wants the development of a core component to be based on agile practices, as the final scope of (the requirement has not yet been fully developed. The project manager is participating in contract development with the sales team and wants to ensure that development costs do not impact the profitability of the project. Which two controls should the project manager incorporate into the contract to specifically address the development of the core component? (Choose two) *

o.t: Limit the number of iterations for development in the contract.
Establish a governance committee to review the contract delivery.
Tier the contract for fixed and agile components.
Provide alternatives to scope change at specific project phases within the contract.
Require that only internal resources be utilized for this project.

questions.e: A. Limit the number of iterations for development in the contract: This control helps manage the time and cost associated with the agile development of the core component. By limiting the number of iterations, the project manager can ensure that the development stays within the fixed budget and timeline, preventing scope creep. C. Tier the contract for fixed and agile components: This approach allows the project to separate the fixed scope and budget components from the agile components. It provides clarity on which parts of the project are flexible and iterative, and which parts are not, helping to manage costs and expectations more effectively.

questions.q: How should the project manager develop the project management plan to ensure that the project continually delivers the expected benefits? *

o.t: Clarify project benefits with the sponsor.
Identify the goal of each work product.
Perform integration testing of each release.
Include the entire project team in testing.

questions.e: Clarifying project benefits with the sponsor ensures that the project management plan is aligned with the overall goals and expected outcomes of the project. This alignment helps in continually delivering the expected benefits throughout the project lifecycle, as it keeps the focus on what is most important to the stakeholders and sponsor.

questions.q: A company's new communication system will include online dashboard reporting. The executive board might receive bi-weekly performance reports through the online dashboard. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Review the project management plan.
Update the stakeholder engagement plan.
Update the communications management plan.
Review the configuration management plan.

questions.e: The communications management plan outlines how information will be communicated to stakeholders, including the frequency, method, and format of communications. Since the executive board will receive bi-weekly performance reports through the online dashboard, the project manager should update the communications management plan to reflect this new reporting method and ensure that all stakeholders are informed and aligned with the updated communication processes.

questions.q: An organization has recently decided to switch from a predictive to an agile delivery approach. The one ongoing project will still be led by a project manager. The agile teams for that project have not produced any documentation. What should the project manager of the ongoing project do? *

o.t: Submit new user stories to the product owner in order to put documentation in the product backlog.
Introduce a document management tool to support the agile teams in preparing the documentation.
Check with the agile teams to see if the project manager's understanding of the Agile Manifesto is correct.
Add an additional team member to take up the role of scribe for the required documentation.

questions.e: Introducing a document management tool will help the agile teams efficiently create and manage necessary documentation. This approach aligns with agile practices by providing a practical tool to facilitate documentation without overwhelming the team, ensuring that important project information is captured and maintained.

questions.q: A team member is hosting an event and invites several colleagues through their work calendars. Another team member, who was not invited to the event, is noticeably distracted during several standup meetings. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Ask the individual who is hosting the event to use private communication methods.
Set up a meeting with the distracted team member to discuss any issues.
Add a social events section to the charter to handle these situations.
Ask the individual who is hosting the event to mark it as private.

questions.e: Setting up a meeting with the distracted team member to discuss any issues directly addresses the root cause of the distraction. It allows the project manager to understand the team member's concerns, offer support, and find a resolution. This approach promotes open communication and ensures that any underlying issues are addressed, contributing to a more cohesive and focused team environment.
