questions.q: A group has been working together for one month. During daily meetings a team member continues to express issues in completing their tasks. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Wait for the team to identify and solve the problem independently.
Move the team member to another task that is more skill appropriate.
Have a confidential discussion with the team member to identify the root cause.
Start a discussion with all team members to help resolve the issues.

questions.e: Having a confidential discussion with the team member allows the project manager to understand the specific challenges the team member is facing. This approach respects the individual's privacy and provides an opportunity to address any personal or professional issues that may be affecting their performance. Once the root cause is identified, appropriate support or adjustments can be made to help the team member succeed in their tasks.

questions.q: One of a project manager’s team members is continuously improving. This team member has been a role model and mentor to others in the organization. How should the project manager acknowledge this team member’s commitment? *

o.t: Send this person to a meeting to negotiate the scope with the client.
Appreciate this team member’s performance throughout the project life cycle.
Promote this team member to a coaching role after this project is completed.
Document it in the team member’s end of year performance review.

questions.e: Acknowledging the team member's performance consistently throughout the project life cycle provides ongoing recognition and motivation. This continuous appreciation helps maintain high morale and reinforces positive behavior. It also demonstrates the project manager's recognition of the team member's contributions in real-time, which can be more impactful than a one-time acknowledgment.

questions.q: The project manager is having difficulty obtaining approval of the project requirements because there is disagreement among the project stakeholders. This issue is putting the project schedule at risk. What should the project manager do first to facilitate the approval of project requirements? *

o.t: Review the project charter.
Perform a stakeholder analysis.
Identify the source of the disagreement.
Hold a team-building event.

questions.e: Identifying the source of the disagreement among stakeholders is the first step in resolving the issue. Understanding the root cause of the disagreement allows the project manager to address specific concerns, mediate discussions, and find common ground. This approach is crucial for facilitating the approval of project requirements and keeping the project on schedule.

questions.q: A project manager is assigned to lead a newly formed agile team. The functional manager has assigned tasks to team members, but the team members do not feel empowered. How can the project manager promote empowerment and accountability among the team? *

o.t: Assign the tasks individually based on the role of the team member to ensure expertise on the subject.
Encourage and assign the team to perform demos of their products or software with the customers.
Give the team autonomy to make their own decisions on how to perform the tasks.
Encourage the team to keep the product owner involved when choosing ways to resolve the given task.

questions.e: Granting the team autonomy to make their own decisions on how to perform tasks is a fundamental principle of agile methodologies. It promotes empowerment and accountability by allowing team members to take ownership of their work and make decisions collectively. This approach helps build trust, fosters creativity, and enhances the team's ability to deliver high-quality results.

questions.q: A project manager identifies an issue between two team members that is affecting the development of one of the deliverables during the second iteration of a project. How should the project manager address this issue to avoid any impact to the project? *

o.t: Contact the functional managers to request substitutes for the conflicting team members.
Send a warning to both team members indicating that if the issue continues, both will be removed from the project.
Schedule a meeting with both team members to understand the issue and facilitate a solution that satisfies both parties.
Escalate both team members to their respective functional managers and let them take the appropriate actions.

questions.e: Scheduling a meeting with both team members to understand the issue and facilitate a solution promotes open communication and conflict resolution. This approach helps address the root cause of the problem, fosters collaboration, and ensures that the project continues without disruption. It also demonstrates the project manager's commitment to team cohesion and effective problem-solving.

questions.q: A self-organizing team was delivering as committed. The team accepted a development task with new technology and the iterations started to have reduced velocity. What management decision is suited for this situation? *

o.t: Provide opportunity for team members to learn and adjust to the technology.
Move team members who are not performing from the team.
Add new members to the team and increase the velocity.
Re-assign the project to a team that has worked with this technology.

questions.e: When a team encounters reduced velocity due to new technology, the best approach is to provide opportunities for team members to learn and adapt. This supports their growth and development, allows the team to become proficient with the new technology, and ultimately improves long-term performance without disrupting team dynamics.

questions.q: A project manager is leading an in-house company project in its very early stages. This current project is similar to another project that ended a year ago. What should the project manager do to analyze the involved stakeholders? *

o.t: Lower the priority of stakeholder engagement as the stakeholders already have knowledge of this kind of project.
Use lessons learned from the previous project as a guide for the current project's stakeholder register.
Refer to the stakeholder register from the previous project as it was similar to the current project.
Document in the risk register that the current project may have different stakeholders than the previous project.

questions.e: Using lessons learned from the previous project as a guide for the current project's stakeholder register allows the project manager to leverage past experiences while considering any changes or differences in the new project. This approach ensures that stakeholder analysis is informed by previous insights but remains tailored to the current project's unique context and needs.

questions.q: During the execution of a financial project, a project manager met with the project team weekly to evaluate the project's progress. However, the sponsor requests that project performance be checked daily. The key team members disagree with this requirement and argue that they do not have enough time to go to daily meetings because they are at an executive level. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Negotiate with the key team members to send a daily report and let the sponsor know that the project cost will increase. ty
Recommend to the sponsor that performance of the project be reviewed once per week.
Review the communications management plan and submit a change request if required.
Evaluate the capacity of each team member to attend daily meetings in person or virtually and reduce the time of each meeting.

questions.e: The communications management plan outlines how project information will be communicated to stakeholders. Reviewing this plan helps the project manager determine if the sponsor's request aligns with the agreed communication strategy. If necessary, the project manager can submit a change request to update the plan, ensuring that the communication needs of both the sponsor and the team are met without significantly impacting the project's progress or team capacity.

questions.q: An agile project team discovers that they are unable to implement a feature completely in the first iteration. The team believes it may not be able to complete the tasks in the second iteration. The feature is a critical component that the customer has prioritized. What should the team do?

o.t: Go back to the customer and explain that they cannot implement the feature completely in one iteration.
Reduce the scope of the feature to fit into one iteration and deliver it to the customer.
Ask the customer to simplify the feature so that it can be implemented in one iteration.
Split the feature into smaller sub-features. implement them, and then deliver them incrementally in multiple iterations.

questions.e: n agile methodology, breaking down a large or complex feature into smaller, manageable sub-features allows the team to make continuous progress and deliver value incrementally. This approach ensures that parts of the critical component can be delivered and reviewed by the customer in each iteration, maintaining momentum and improving the overall delivery process. It also aligns with agile principles of iterative development and continuous feedback.

questions.q: During a project review meeting, several project team members expressed that they did not have an understanding of the benefits of certain features for the project. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Review the project scope statement.
Confirm ownership for ongoing value realization.
Escalate the issue to the project sponsor.
Appraise the stakeholders of value gain progress.

questions.e: Reviewing the project scope statement can help clarify the intended benefits and objectives of the project features. This document outlines the project's deliverables and the work required to complete them, providing the team with a clear understanding of the project's goals and how each feature contributes to achieving those goals. This step ensures that all team members are aligned and understand the value of their work within the context of the project.

questions.q: A food company is developing a new product using a predictive approach, and the product is currently in the testing phase. Given the nature of the feedback of the tests, the project manager has decided to use an iterative approach. At the end of one of the iterations, a new regulation related to the product is enacted. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Make a change request regarding the project's scope to ensure compliance.
Include an assessment to verify compliance in the next iteration.
Conduct an iteration review to address the new regulation.
Start the tests over, adapting the trials to the new regulation.

questions.e: This approach allows the project team to incorporate the regulatory requirements into their ongoing work without disrupting the overall flow of the project. It also ensures that compliance is considered early in the iteration, which helps in mitigating any potential risks associated with the new regulation.

questions.q: A project manager is assigned to a technical research project. The project team has already been assigned, and the main subject matter expert (SME) sends the project manager a list of the technical skills required for the execution of this project. What should the project manager do next?

o.t: Send the list to the project team and ask them to get training on the required skills.
Ask the functional manager to review the resource pool and recommend the right individuals to join the team.
Discuss the list with the project sponsor to confirm that the resources have the required skills.
Meet with the project team to understand their skills and identify potential gaps and training requirements.

questions.e: Meeting with the project team to understand their current skills and identify potential gaps is crucial for ensuring the project is executed effectively. This approach allows the project manager to assess the team's capabilities, determine any necessary training or additional resources, and develop a plan to address any skill gaps. It ensures that the team is adequately prepared to meet the technical requirements of the project.

questions.q: During the third iteration of a project, the main sponsor retired from the company, and a new sponsor was appointed. The new sponsor is not familiar with the agile approach for project delivery, which leads them to request more control over the project team. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Schedule a meeting with the new sponsor in order to explain the agile approach and how teams are supposed to be self-organized.
Schedule an emergency meeting with the project team so they fulfill every request that comes from the sponsor.
Review the sponsor's request with the project team during the next daily review meeting in order to provide the requested control.
Review the sponsor's request with the project team during the next iteration review meeting in order to obtain a team decision.

questions.e: When a new sponsor who is not familiar with the agile approach requests more control over the project team, it is crucial to educate them about the principles and practices of agile methodology. Agile teams are designed to be self-organized and empowered to make decisions. By scheduling a meeting with the new sponsor, the project manager can explain how agile works, the benefits of self-organization, and how it contributes to the project's success. This understanding will help the sponsor support the agile process and avoid unnecessary interference that could disrupt the team's workflow.

questions.q: A new team member is added to a self-organizing team. The new team member is reluctant to speak and take part in team discussions or decisions. Which two actions should the team take to engage this new team member? (Choose two) *

o.t: Revisit the team's discussion on team behaviors and norms.
Report to the project manager about the new team member’s behavior.
Coach the new team member to improve engagement with the team.
Force the new team member to participate in activities that are considered easy.
Facilitate an open discussion on all ideas and perspectives.

questions.e: A. Revisit the team's discussion on team behaviors and norms: Revisiting the team's behaviors and norms helps ensure that everyone, including new members, understands the expectations and culture of the team. This creates an environment where the new team member feels comfortable and understands how they are expected to engage. C. Coach the new team member to improve engagement with the team: Coaching the new team member can help them build confidence and understand their role within the team. It provides personalized support and guidance to help them become an active participant in team discussions and decisions. These actions foster an inclusive team environment and provide the new member with the support they need to integrate effectively into the team.

questions.q: The project manager of an agile project has been asked to reduce the budget by 30% Since this is a small project team, the budget is primarily allocated to resources. What strategy should the project manager use in order to keep delivering value in a restricted environment? *

o.t: Reduce the project staff and adjust the scope and timelines accordingly in support of the budget reduction.
Balance the project team in order to accommodate the budget challenges and provide training to mitigate the risk of low performance.
Prioritize the product backlog looking for high business value and low effort and adjust the project budget and staffing to account for those items.
Restrict the project scope only to basic critical features and run the project with the current staffing level until all of the budget is consumed.

questions.e: In an agile project, focusing on delivering the highest value with the least effort is crucial when facing budget constraints. By prioritizing the product backlog, the project manager can ensure that the team works on items that provide the most business value relative to their cost. This approach helps maximize the return on investment and maintain project momentum even with reduced resources. Adjusting the budget and staffing to align with these high-priority items ensures that the project continues to deliver value despite financial restrictions.

questions.q: A business stakeholder for a project is reluctant to accept an agile approach due to a previous bad experience and is pushing for a predictive approach. What strategy should the project manager use to persuade the stakeholder to use an agile approach? *

o.t: Propose a phased project approach with multiple small interactions and build trust with the stakeholder through frequent value delivery.
Document the request and escalate to upper management to consider a modification of the project charter.
Agree on a predictive approach but apply agile concepts under the project management umbrella.
Ensure the stakeholder that an agile approach will deliver all of the expected results in a shorter period of time.

questions.e: When a business stakeholder is reluctant to accept an agile approach due to past experiences, it is essential to build trust gradually. By proposing a phased approach with multiple small iterations, the project manager can demonstrate the value of agile through frequent, tangible deliveries. This approach helps to mitigate the stakeholder's concerns by showing quick wins and continuous improvement, thereby building trust and confidence in the agile process over time. This strategy aligns with agile principles and addresses the stakeholder's need for predictability and control.

questions.q: In an advanced stage of a project a stakeholder who is not receiving the project status report communicates this to the project manager. After checking, the project manager determines that the person is registered as a stakeholder but was not included in the communications management plan. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Update the communications management plan to include the missed stakeholder and send the current project status documentation to this stakeholder.
Inform the project sponsor that there are stakeholders who are not included in the communications management plan.
Inform the stakeholder that the project team cannot provide information to anyone who is not registered in the project's communications management plan.
Ask the stakeholder to get the project status report from another stakeholder listed in the communications management plan.

questions.e: When a stakeholder is identified as not receiving the necessary communications, the project manager should update the communications management plan to ensure that all relevant stakeholders are included. Sending the current project status documentation to the missed stakeholder immediately addresses their need for information and prevents any further miscommunication. This action ensures that the stakeholder is kept informed and engaged with the project moving forward.

questions.q: On a transformational project, the project manager is confronted with resistance from the stakeholders. To overcome this and gain acceptance of the change. What should the project manager do first? *

o.t: Escalate the issue to the project sponsor.
Review the stakeholder engagement plan.
Update the issue log.
Neutralize the negative stakeholders.

questions.e: When confronted with resistance from stakeholders, the project manager should first review the stakeholder engagement plan. This plan outlines strategies for engaging stakeholders and managing their expectations and concerns. By reviewing it, the project manager can identify the specific reasons for resistance and adjust engagement strategies accordingly. This approach allows for a targeted response to the resistance, fostering better communication and increasing the chances of gaining stakeholder acceptance for the change.

questions.q: A multinational company has a plan to expand their business into a new country where they currently have no presence. A project manager is assigned to initiate this project. After reviewing the business case, what should be considered first when developing an appropriate implementation strategy? *

o.t: Acquire project resources from the new country to mitigate the risk of uncertainty.
Evaluate the environmental and regulatory factors and identify high-level risks and assumptions.
Identify and monitor the risks closely since the company does not have lessons learned for this country.
Ensure that project sponsors are in agreement on the project deliverables and timeline during the project.

questions.e: When expanding into a new country, it's crucial to first understand the environmental and regulatory factors that could impact the project. These factors include local laws, regulations, cultural differences, economic conditions, and political stability. By evaluating these factors and identifying high-level risks and assumptions, the project manager can develop a more informed and appropriate implementation strategy, ensuring that potential challenges are recognized and mitigated early in the project. This approach helps in aligning the project with the new country’s specific requirements and reducing the risk of unforeseen obstacles.

questions.q: A project team is having difficulties understanding technical details regarding requirements. The information was not initially provided by the customer, but the information is critical in the current iteration for clarification on how tasks need to be accomplished. How should the project manager approach this situation? *

o.t: Request that the customer reviews and clarifies feature definitions for the current sprint.
Send a burndown chart of the current sprint to the customer and seek clarifications.
Educate the customer and have them participate in daily standup meetings.
Schedule weekly meetings and product reviews with the customer to clarify requirements.

questions.e: When the project team needs clarification on technical details regarding requirements that were not initially provided, it is crucial to address this promptly to ensure the current iteration's success. Requesting that the customer reviews and clarifies the feature definitions for the current sprint directly addresses the immediate need for information. This approach ensures that the team gets the necessary details to proceed with their tasks and helps maintain the sprint's progress and deliverables on track.

questions.q: A project manager has been managing a project for several months when an issue that had not been registered as a risk appeared. This issue may have a big impact on the project. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Delay the project until the issue is addressed and no longer presents as a risk to the project.
Inform the sponsor that the issue has arisen, and that the project's success may be uncertain.
Avoid managing the issue as it was not registered as a risk for the project and there is no planned response to it.
Hold a meeting with the project team and relevant stakeholders to agree on the best way to manage the issue.

questions.e: When an unforeseen issue arises that may significantly impact the project, the project manager should promptly address it by involving the project team and relevant stakeholders. Holding a meeting allows for a collective discussion to understand the issue's implications, brainstorm possible solutions, and agree on the best course of action. This collaborative approach ensures that the issue is managed effectively and that the project can continue with minimal disruption.

questions.q: A project leader of an agile team realizes that one team member is unmotivated, which is affecting the whole team. What should the project leader do to improve the situation? *

o.t: Invest in developing the team's emotional intelligence.
Ask the unmotivated team member to take a short leave.
Reduce the number of daily and retrospective meetings.
Send the unmotivated team member to another team.

questions.e: Investing in the development of the team's emotional intelligence can help address the root causes of the unmotivated team member's behavior and improve the overall team dynamics. Emotional intelligence training can enhance team members' ability to understand and manage their own emotions, as well as empathize with and support their colleagues. This approach can create a more positive and productive work environment, helping to re-engage the unmotivated team member and improve the morale and performance of the entire team.

questions.q: A project manager who is managing a critical project in a multinational company is conducting a progress meeting with all team members. During the meeting, one of the team members states that they are facing a critical problem that will prevent them from completing their assigned task. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Ask the team member to follow the approved communications management plan to communicate their issue.
Schedule a meeting with the concerned team member to review and update the issue log together.
Review the risk register with the team member to find the proper response action for this issue.
Ask the team member to raise a change request to assess the issue in detail.

questions.e: Scheduling a meeting to review and update the issue log ensures that the problem is documented, assessed, and addressed systematically. This action allows the project manager to understand the details of the issue, determine its impact, and collaborate with the team member to find a solution. It also ensures that the issue is tracked and managed properly, facilitating better communication and resolution.

questions.q: During a sprint planning meeting, a stakeholder is told that their requirement is in progress and on track for the final product to be ready in the next two sprints. The stakeholder is very satisfied with the timeline and gives their full support to the agile team. After the meeting, the project sponsor calls the project manager about a large requirement they want the team to work on right away as it has significant business value. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Call the stakeholder to tell them that the final product schedule must be extended due to this last minute, urgent request.
Perform an impact analysis and share the overall schedule impact before deciding on a new priority.
Reject the new requirement from the sponsor as this is going to impact the delivery of the stakeholder's final product.
Ask the product owner to prioritize the new request from the sponsor and ask the team to work on it immediately.

questions.e: When faced with a new, urgent request from the project sponsor, the project manager should first perform an impact analysis to understand how this new requirement will affect the current schedule, including the delivery of existing commitments. By analyzing the impact, the project manager can provide a clear picture of the trade-offs involved. This information can then be shared with the product owner, stakeholders, and the sponsor to make an informed decision on how to prioritize the new request. This approach ensures that all parties are aware of the potential implications and can agree on the best course of action based on the project's overall goals and priorities.

questions.q: A geographically distributed project team has development issues between the collocated and virtual teams causing productivity to decrease. What should the project manager do to address this issue? *

o.t: Force the team members to work from one location.
Develop protocols for resolving conflicts between team members.
Obtain special expertise to advise the team members.
Set up face-to-face meetings with project team members.

questions.e: Developing protocols for resolving conflicts provides a structured approach to addressing and managing conflicts within the team. It helps ensure that team members have clear guidelines on how to handle disagreements and issues, promoting a collaborative and productive environment. This approach is practical for a geographically distributed team as it does not require physical presence and focuses on improving team dynamics and communication.

questions.q: A project manager is assigned to a new marketing campaign. The sponsor gives the project manager an approved project management plan for review and explains the scope, business requirements, deliverables and stakeholders. The project manager asks to see the project charter to gain a better understanding of the project. The sponsor says the project is small and simple so there is no need for a project charter. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Speak with peers about the need for a project charter.
Develop the project charter and send it for approval.
Explain that a project charter is necessary to ensure agreement on scope and deliverables and to define the project manager's responsibilities.
Agree that the project does not require a project charter, especially since the deliverables and milestones are included in the project management plan.

questions.e: The project charter is a crucial document that formally authorizes the project and provides a clear definition of its objectives, scope, stakeholders, and the project manager's authority. By explaining the importance of the project charter to the sponsor, the project manager can ensure that there is a mutual understanding of the project's purpose, scope, and deliverables, and that their role and responsibilities are clearly defined. This helps prevent misunderstandings and provides a solid foundation for project execution.

questions.q: A stakeholder on a project has a reputation for being easily angered and unreasonably difficult on projects. The project manager would like to minimize the impact of the stakeholder’s behavior on the development team. What training should the project manager choose for their team to help with this situation? *

o.t: Communication training.
Negotiation training.
Emotional intelligence training.
Agile training.

questions.e: Emotional intelligence training can help the project team better manage their interactions with the difficult stakeholder. This type of training focuses on improving self-awareness, self-regulation, social awareness, and relationship management. By developing these skills, team members can better understand and manage their own emotions and respond more effectively to the stakeholder's behavior. This can help minimize the impact of the stakeholder’s behavior on the team and improve overall team dynamics and performance.

questions.q: A key project stakeholder showed interest in the beginning of a complex agile project but has become less involved as the sprint has progressed due to additional responsibilities. A few sprints later, the key stakeholder rejected a feature deliverable. The team is reworking the rejected deliverable for the next sprint. What should the project manager have done to avoid this situation? *

o.t: Involved the key stakeholders in the decision-making process.
Customized stakeholder communications based on the stakeholders’ needs.
Analyzed the changes in stakeholder attributes.
Documented the project vision and objectives.

questions.e: This approach helps in maintaining their interest and involvement, especially when their availability changes due to additional responsibilities. Effective communication tailored to stakeholders' needs can prevent misunderstandings and ensure that stakeholders are aligned with the project's progress and deliverables, thereby avoiding situations where deliverables are rejected due to lack of involvement.

questions.q: During initiation of a new product improvement project, a project manager finds historical data showing that a similar project resulted in customers complaining of an even worse user experience compared to the previous product version. How can the project manager prevent this outcome in the new project? *

o.t: Hire a team of external users to perform acceptance testing on the product.
Define a user focus group as external stakeholders with a high influence on outcomes.
Hire a consultant to perform a benefit analysis as an input to the project charter.
Define a high-level risk and plan mitigation after completing the work breakdown structure (WBS).

questions.e: By defining a user focus group with high influence, the project manager ensures that real users' needs, preferences, and feedback are taken into account throughout the project. This proactive approach helps in identifying potential issues early and aligning the product improvements with user expectations, thereby improving the likelihood of a positive user experience.

questions.q: An agile project team is building a new product. The stakeholders require ongoing illustration of project business value. How should the project manager proceed? *

o.t: Prepare performance value reports for the business on an ongoing basis.
Include demonstrations of the built portion of the product at the end of every sprint.
Prepare a project report for the stakeholders and distribute it weekly.
Confirm the minimum viable product (MVP) and demonstrate it to the business when it is ready.

questions.e: In an agile project, demonstrating the built portions of the product at the end of every sprint, often referred to as a "sprint review" or "demo," allows stakeholders to see the ongoing progress and the business value being delivered incrementally. This approach keeps stakeholders engaged and informed, provides them with regular opportunities to give feedback, and ensures that the product development aligns with their expectations. Regular demonstrations help illustrate the project's business value and facilitate better communication and collaboration between the team and stakeholders.

questions.q: During the execution of a project the project manager notices that only one team member has one of the technical skills needed to build the product. The project manager is afraid this might have a future impact on the quality and schedule because most of the upcoming activities will require at least three people with this specific skill. What two actions should the project manager take to prevent the team from being unqualified? (Choose two) *

o.t: Exclude the activities from the roadmap.
Encourage working in pairs and knowledge sharing.
Teach the entire team the new skill.
Facilitate a training event with an external trainer.
Increase the time estimates on the activities that require such abilities.

questions.e: B. Encourage working in pairs and knowledge sharing: Pair programming or similar collaborative approaches allow the team member with the required skill to share their knowledge with other team members. This helps build the team's overall capability and reduces dependency on a single individual. D. Facilitate a training event with an external trainer: Bringing in an external trainer to provide specialized training can quickly upskill multiple team members. This ensures that more team members acquire the necessary technical skill, thereby mitigating the risk to quality and schedule. These actions help ensure the team is adequately skilled and can handle the upcoming activities, maintaining both the quality and schedule of the project.

questions.q: A project manager has been managing a highly complex project. The project manager has ensured that all of the required tasks have been completed. During a recent external audit. The project manager was informed of a heavy penalty being levied on the project for the latest module that was implemented. What should the project manager have done to ensure that there were no liabilities arising from the recent implementation? *

o.t: Ensured that all defects identified during testing were resolved before implementation.
Ensured that all of the required tasks identified in the scope were completed successfully.
Ensured that all documentation was completed post implementation before closing the project.
Ensured that all the required approvals were received per the organizational procedures.

questions.e: By securing the appropriate approvals, the project manager can verify that all aspects of the project, including compliance and risk management, have been thoroughly reviewed and validated. This step helps to mitigate the risk of penalties and other liabilities associated with the project implementation.
